raw.title: Mission 02 — Stablecoin — Season II

labels.name: source:h2
labels.description: Demand exposed by Telegraph Hackathon Season II

raw.body:
**Start with the customer and work backwards.** This mission is about delivering something useful, not accumulating disconnected Intents or registrations. A contributor can build the whole solution—application, intelligence Provider and relevant evaluation work—or concentrate on one part and work with others. All three hackathon tracks are open, with separate qualifying entries under the [official rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules).

## The opportunity

**Who it serves:** Stablecoin issuers, payment operators and on-chain credit/treasury teams.

**Problem:** Agent payments and wallet-based compliance are poorly represented in existing finance and reporting tools.

**A useful result:** An auditable machine-payment/treasury workflow with transaction accounting, controls, evidence and a verifiable result.

Pick a specific customer and workflow. Establish the alternative they use today, a realistic willingness-to-pay or budget constraint, a measurable result, acceptable error and response time. These are example opportunities, not exclusive products or confirmed customers. See [Stablecoin](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions/stablecoin) and the [full mission catalogue](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions).

| Route | Actual outcome to build | Shared capability families to investigate and use |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Agent expense ledger** | Track the actual testnet USDC spend and outcomes of an agent fleet, with spend limits, cost per task and ledger entries tied to receipts. | `CRYPTO_TRANSFER_VERIFY`, `TASK_EXECUTION_QUALITY`, `GAS_PRICE` |
| **2. Compliance before settlement** | Screen a name or wallet and risk signals before authorizing a testnet transfer; make HOLD and UNKNOWN fail closed and retain the evidence. | `SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH`, `TRANSACTION_RISK`, `FRAUD_RISK`, `REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR` |
| **3. Evidence-based treasury decision** | Buy reserve and liquidity evidence, propose or simulate a rebalance, and show precisely which checks caused the decision. | `ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION`, `LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY`, `CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY` |

**First milestone:** one realistic input → a paid Telegraph intelligence request → a checked result with its source/uncertainty → a useful action or answer → receipt and total cost. Include one failure case before expanding the workflow. You do **not** need to implement all three example products.

**Tests worth demonstrating:** Attempt a sanctioned payee, missing/unknown result, insufficient budget and stale or conflicting reserve data; ensure no unauthorized funds move.

**Measures that matter:** Spend and fees per approved settlement, blocked-risk recall, error reconciliation, budget overruns.

## Intelligence needed

**Published starting families:** `ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION`, `SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH`, `FRAUD_RISK`, `TRANSACTION_RISK`, `LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY`, `CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY`, `DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY`, `VESSEL_TELEMETRY_VERIFY`, `FX_NOW`, `PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY`.

These are shared network capabilities, **not separate bounties** created for this mission. The same capability may support several missions, with one canonical Intent, one Provider market and one evaluation pool. The list is a starting map, not a mandatory bill of materials or proof of live coverage.

Before implementing anything, inspect the [live canonical Intent list](https://devnode.telegraphprotocol.com/engine/v1/intents), [request and response schemas](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema), [ranked Providers](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/explore) and [published Intent catalogue](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/INTENTS.md). Use the **exact** live `intent_name` and `request.params`; family names and guessed `_GENERAL` suffixes are not reliable request identifiers. Some unknown names return HTTP 200 with a null schema, which is not a working Intent. The [mission mapping](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/MISSIONS.md) is helpful for discovery, but the node determines which capabilities are callable and what evaluation path applies.

A finished report, dashboard, refund, memo or decision is usually **application composition**, not a new protocol Intent. Use existing reusable capabilities first. Only propose a new Intent for genuinely reusable intelligence missing from the catalogue.

## Ways to contribute

### Apps & Agents — deliver the product

Build a runnable application that **autonomously purchases or sells intelligence through Telegraph** and uses the response to complete a meaningful task. Start with the smallest useful customer workflow; confirm the supporting Intents and live Provider quality before committing to an architecture.

Choose the right [delivery path](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/inference-paths): [Engine Ask](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/engine-ask) for fresh on-demand work; [x402](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/x402-inference) or [escrow](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/escrow-inference) for supported settlement; [WebSocket Signals](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/websocket-signals) when reusable streamed intelligence is appropriate; [MCP](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/mcp-server) for integrations. A Signal subscription is not a substitute for a fresh, user-specific check. A 402 payment challenge is not evidence of a completed purchase.

Make uncertainty visible. Handle partial or conflicting answers, stale data, missing Providers, spending limits and failures. Prove the total **cost per useful completed outcome** rather than multiplying paid requests unnecessarily. Reuse valid fresh intelligence when permitted; avoid paying repeatedly for the same shared fact. Irreversible transactions and sensitive actions require the user's authorization. Simulated or testnet behavior must be labelled as such.

**Completion evidence:** runnable app and instructions, a new realistic input producing a useful result, authentic Telegraph request/payment evidence, costs and latency, and a reproducible failure case. A static interface or a Miner registration alone does not qualify as the app.

### Miners / Providers — supply the intelligence

Identify a missing or weak capability for this customer workflow. Test existing Providers to understand the quality bar. Independent competing implementations for the same canonical Intent are welcome; show how yours performs in accuracy, coverage, freshness, price, reliability or latency. Implement a callable service for a supported canonical Intent, following its actual request/response schema and [Miner YAML guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/yaml-config).

Check the [validation guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/validation-api) and current [registration steps](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/miner-registration). **Known documentation limitation (Nov 15):** the guide says its `POST /dashboard/validate` endpoint currently returns 404; use the available web checks, documented local checks and supported registration dry-run instead of treating that POST as working. Use the [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet) for eligible testnet needs. Confirm the registration is active and the service answers the actual Intent; capture its registration ID, test cases, measured results and paid request evidence. Distinguish direct diagnostic requests from selection by ranked routing.

Share working endpoints and registration IDs here so other applications and missions can reuse the Provider.

### Evaluators — measure whether the intelligence is good

Use the selected Intent's **actual node class, family and scoring path**, not the name or an old bounty description, to determine what's needed:

- **Deterministic:** reliable public truth-source material and the supported comparator path. A new judgment adapter is not inherently required.
- **Hybrid:** the checkable truth source/comparator and judgment contribution that the live scoring path actually uses.
- **Judgment:** sourced, balanced better/worse examples and a compatible evaluation adapter **where needed**. Do not assume every Intent needs a new adapter plus material.

Contribute through [Anjoman Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval), following [material formats and provenance](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/contribute-evaluation-data) and the [scoring-module guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/build-a-scoring-module) when applicable. Use primary evidence, timestamps, block/chain or jurisdiction identifiers, correct units and tolerances. Include correct, incorrect, incomplete and ambiguous cases; avoid datasets solvable merely by answer length, keywords or copied prompt wording. Test on unseen sources and failure types. Confirm **eligible / rejected** material state and actual module status separately; passing a local test or uploading rows does not imply canonical promotion.

A single project may contribute a working app, a Provider and genuinely useful evaluation work. Each track still requires its own qualifying evidence. No extra or duplicative component is needed simply to claim participation across all three.

## Share work here as it happens

**Read the latest comments and existing [Bounties Issues](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/issues) to understand current activity, available capabilities and opportunities to collaborate.** Multiple contributors are welcome to independently build applications, Providers and Evaluators for the same mission or Intent, including competing implementations. Existing work does not reserve a mission, product or Intent. Share progress and findings so others can collaborate, reuse useful contributions or compete independently.

If using the existing Bounties workflow, post `/claim` and then a short comment identifying your scope. Claims are **non-exclusive**. Keep the thread current with `/progress <update>` at least every **72 hours** while claimed, and link relevant work from other mission threads. Useful updates include:

```text
Scope: [product or capability + customer problem]
Track(s): [Apps & Agents / Miners / Providers / Evaluators]
Working on: [concrete deliverable, canonical Intents if known]
Reusing (optional): [existing work, Providers, evaluations + links]
Approach: [what you are building and how you plan to deliver it]
Current state: [building / tested / blocked / submitted]
Proof or next milestone: [repo/demo/endpoint, reproducible result]
```

When ready, post `/submit <links and evidence>` for your individual contribution, **and** use the official Anjoman submission path. GitHub comments coordinate work; they are not the final hackathon entry or evaluation upload. One team's submission does not close the mission to other participants. Existing accepted contributions and claims remain valid; reviewers assess individual entries separately. Don't post credentials, private customer data, protected evaluation samples or sensitive exploit details.

## Prove it, share it, submit it

A strong entry can be tested by someone outside the team: provide a live demo or callable endpoint, public-safe repository, run instructions, real request IDs/receipts, one failure test, honest cost figures and limitations. For apps, explain what was purchased and **what useful action happened afterward**. Consider listing working apps in [Anjoman Apps](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/apps) for others to discover.

The [Season II judging rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules) apply across all three tracks (100 points each; **70/100** overall and each track's stated technical minimum). Apps are scored on technical quality/mainnet readiness (35 points, minimum 24), commercial viability (25), independent adoption (10), integration and usage (5), reproducibility (5), and organic growth/developer activation (20). Providers and Evaluators have their **own** track rubrics on the same rules page.

The 20 growth points cover **useful education (5), ease of adoption (5), organic distribution (5), and independent community activation (5)**. Share a working explanation or video, a genuinely useful walkthrough, and **at least three meaningful original progress updates on separate dates**. Invite independent developers to try, reproduce or integrate your work; show their real feedback and results. Publish where relevant (GitHub, Discord, X, technical communities) and follow the published tagging/link guidance. Bought engagement, fake traffic, manipulated stars, self-dealing and fabricated demand do not count. **Star the [Bounties repository](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties)** as required in Section 5; this is an entry requirement, not proof of growth.

**Prizes and possible earnings:** $7,000 for the Season II main competition ($3,000 Apps, $2,000 Providers, $2,000 Evaluators), plus $3,000 reserved for separate December challenges—not an extra automatic Season II pool. Awards depend on eligibility and verification. Beyond prizes, eligible Providers may earn from paid usage, Evaluator contributions may earn applicable protocol rewards, and products may generate revenue if customers adopt them. **Nothing is guaranteed** by a claim, registration or testnet call. This is a coordination Issue, not a separately funded GitHub bounty.

**Deadline:** **December 1, 2026, 23:59 UTC** for the main competition; **November 20** is the progress showcase. Finish the [official H2 submission](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon) using its live form when available, selecting the tracks and attaching distinct evidence for each. As of November 15, the site says the final form opens later; don't mistake a GitHub `/submit` comment for the final submission. The official rules control eligibility, awards, dates and any subsequent announcements.

## Before reporting a blocker

| Problem | Check first |
|---|---|
| Intent request fails or returns an empty schema | Select an exact live canonical Intent; inspect `request.params`, response fields and active Provider coverage in the [schema guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema). A 200 response with `request: null` is not a valid Intent. |
| No result after x402 or escrow | Follow the documented full payment flow; a 402 offer alone is not a settled purchase. Check available receipt and account evidence. |
| A Miner looks highly ranked but answers the wrong question | Reproduce the input, preserve the raw/shaped result and actual receipt, compare with a direct diagnostic call, and report the specific ranking gap. |
| Registration, validation or bond trouble | Check the registration and validation docs, live node state, chain configuration and [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet); the documented `POST /dashboard/validate` route is currently flagged as broken. |
| Evaluation material or module rejected | Check eligible/rejected reasons, provenance, required shape, supported family kind and public scoring requirements; don't infer adapter requirements from an Intent's label. |
| A similar app or capability already exists | Independent competing implementations are welcome. Review existing work for useful references, reuse or collaborate where appropriate, or proceed independently. No exclusive claims. |

For a genuine unresolved protocol defect, post a concise reproducible report here (exact Intent, public request, expected/actual behavior and safe evidence), then use [Discord](https://discord.gg/telegraphprotocol) for escalation if necessary.

## Done when

- [ ] A real customer need and runnable app/agent that solves it are demonstrated.
- [ ] A supported paid Telegraph request/sale leads to a useful action, with authentic receipt/accounting evidence.
- [ ] Relevant shared Intents have usable Provider supply and evaluation coverage, or precisely documented remaining gaps.
- [ ] A reviewer can reproduce a realistic success and failure case, including total cost and latency.
- [ ] Contributors' progress and relevant final entries are linked in comments; evidence distinguishes testnet, production and genuine external adoption.

This checklist measures **mission coverage**, not one person's prize eligibility. A successful app does not imply every possible workflow or every mapped Intent is complete. Keep this Issue available for distinct contributors; do not close it merely because one scope finished.

## Reward

**No standalone GitHub payout.** Season II prizes and ongoing protocol earnings are separate and governed by their published eligibility and payment terms.

raw.body:
<!-- bounty-board:body -->
Welcome! These are the open PyHealth bounties: models, datasets, tasks and tools we'd love help adding. Anyone can take one on.

**Before you start**
1. Join the [PyHealth Discord](https://discord.gg/mpb835EHaX). Ask questions and request reviews there.
2. Read the [contribution guide](https://pyhealth.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how_to_contribute.html).

**Pick a bounty**
- Choose the highest-priority bounty you can take on. Priority: ⏫︎ highest, ▲ high, ━ medium, ▼ low, ⏬︎ lowest.
- Pick one marked *To be claimed*. To help with a claimed one, ask in Discord.
- Check that it isn't already in PyHealth or in an [open pull request](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/pulls).
- Know a paper with public code that would fit PyHealth? Suggest it in Discord.

**Claim and build**
- Claim a bounty by opening a pull request (a draft is fine) with its ID in the title, like `[BTY-<id>] <short description>`. `[Bounty-<id>]` works too. This board updates within an hour.
- Your claim holds while the PR is open and after it merges. Closing it without merging releases the bounty.
- Build from the paper's official code, use datasets PyHealth already loads where possible, and aim to reproduce the paper's results.
- Every bounty needs an implementation that follows the [contribution guide](https://pyhealth.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how_to_contribute.html).
- When it's ready, comment `/review` on your PR for an AI review, or ask in Discord.

**Why contribute**
Students in the DL4H course can earn extra credit. Contributors who complete a bounty may get the chance to join a research paper and work with our industry partners.

*This board is generated from [`bounty.yaml`](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/HEAD/bounty.yaml) and updated hourly. Edits made here are overwritten.*

Open bounties: 56 (8 claimed, 48 unclaimed).

## Unclaimed

### Dataset

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-24 · Cardiology Dataset PyHealth 2.0 Migration · To be claimed

Move CardiologyDataset (CPSC 2018, Georgia, PTB, PTB-XL, INCART) onto the 2.0 BaseDataset and keep cardiology_detect working, using TUEV as the reference port. Check open PRs #1052, #1187, and #1323 first to avoid duplicate PTB-XL work. [code1](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/master/pyhealth/datasets/cardiology.py), [code2](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/master/pyhealth/datasets/tuev.py)

### Task

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-27 · Add YAIB Benchmarks into PyHealth · To be claimed

Port the YAIB (Yet Another ICU Benchmark) cohorts and tasks (mortality, AKI, sepsis, kidney function, and length of stay) so PyHealth models can be scored against YAIB baselines on MIMIC-IV and eICU. [code](https://github.com/rvandewater/yaib)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-32 · CLIMB Multimodal Task Suite (ICML 2025) · To be claimed

Integrate the CLIMB multimodal benchmark task suite and shared loaders with PyHealth across datasets such as MIMIC-III/IV, MIMIC-CXR, PTB-XL, TUAB, and TUEV. [code](https://github.com/DDVD233/CLIMB), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07667)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-45 · FedWeight Cross-Site Federated EHR Benchmark (npj Digital Medicine 2025) · To be claimed

Add the FedWeight patient density-ratio re-weighting federated learning benchmark across hospital sites on eICU and MIMIC-III. [code](https://github.com/li-lab-mcgill/FedWeight), [paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-025-01661-8)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-48 · NutriSighT Underfeeding Prediction Task (Nature Communications 2025) · To be claimed

Add the ICU underfeeding prediction task for ventilated patients on MIMIC-IV and AmsterdamUMCdb along with the NutriSighT transformer baseline. [code](https://github.com/mjangda3/NutriSighT), [paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66200-1)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-56 · TRACE Intra-Visit Lab Nowcasting (WWW 2025) · To be claimed

Add the intra-visit lab-value nowcasting task on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV along with the TRACE patient-trajectory encoder. [code](https://github.com/Amehi/TRACE), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23072)

#### ▲ · BTY-62 · MEDFAIR Imaging Fairness Benchmark (ICLR 2023) · To be claimed

Add MEDFAIR's group fairness metrics, model-selection criteria, and debiasing baselines for PyHealth's medical imaging tasks. [code](https://github.com/ys-zong/MEDFAIR)

#### ▼ · BTY-73 · ICU Readmission Architecture Benchmark (Scientific Reports 2020) · To be claimed

Add the time-aware attention and sequence model baselines together with the ICU readmission benchmark on MIMIC-III. [code](https://github.com/sebbarb/time_aware_attention)

### Model

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-28 · EviCare (KDD 2026) · To be claimed

Implement EviCare, a deep-model-guided LLM in-context reasoning framework for diagnosis prediction on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV. [code](https://github.com/zhyccc/EviCare), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10455)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-29 · Awaken the Giant / GiantMed (KDD 2026) · To be claimed

Implement Awaken the Giant (GiantMed), a boundary-aware deep-model-guided LLM framework for medication recommendation on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-30 · LLM Code-Embedding Transfer (npj Digital Medicine 2026) · To be claimed

Add LLM-embedding transfer of EHR predictors across coding systems (such as OMOP/ICD to other vocabularies) for cross-coding-system clinical prediction. [code](https://github.com/mkirchler/grasp), [paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-026-02363-5)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-31 · RePrompT (ACL 2026) · To be claimed

Implement RePrompT (recurrent prompt tuning integrating structured EHR encoders with LLMs), along with RASPER and ARCI baselines, on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV. [code](https://github.com/KU-AI4H/RePrompT), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17725)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-33 · Context Clues Long-Context EHR Foundation Models (ICLR 2025) · To be claimed

Add long-context EHR foundation models (Mamba, Hyena, Llama, GPT) from Context Clues and evaluate them head-to-head against PyHealth's EHRMamba on EHRSHOT and OMOP. [code](https://github.com/som-shahlab/hf_ehr), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16178)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-34 · Delphi-2M (Nature 2025) · To be claimed

Port the Delphi generative transformer for multi-disease next-event and time-to-event prediction with a MIMIC-IV/MEDS port alongside the credentialed UK Biobank setup. [code](https://github.com/gerstung-lab/Delphi), [paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09529-3)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-35 · FLAME (NeurIPS 2025) · To be claimed

Implement FLAME for fine-grained list-wise LLM medication recommendation on PyHealth's MIMIC-III/IV and eICU drug-recommendation tasks alongside SafeDrug, GAMENet, MICRON, and MoleRec. [code](https://github.com/cxfann/Flame), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20218)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-36 · MAESTRO (NeurIPS 2025) · To be claimed

Implement MAESTRO, an adaptive sparse-attention multimodal time-series model, for PyHealth's MIMIC-III multimodal tasks. [code](https://github.com/payalmohapatra/MAESTRO), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25278)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-37 · MIRA Medical Time-Series Foundation Model (NeurIPS 2025) · To be claimed

Integrate MIRA as a medical time-series foundation encoder for PyHealth ICU and biosignal tasks across MIMIC-III/IV, PhysioNet 2012, PTB-XL, and Sleep-EDF. [code](https://github.com/microsoft/MIRA), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07584)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-38 · TarDiff Synthetic EHR Time-Series Generator (KDD 2025) · To be claimed

Implement TarDiff, a target-oriented diffusion framework for generating synthetic EHR time-series data in PyHealth.

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-39 · MedTok Multimodal Code Tokenizer (ICML 2025) · To be claimed

Add MedTok as a drop-in multimodal medical code tokenizer and embedding module for PyHealth EHR models on MIMIC-III/IV and EHRSHOT tasks. [code](https://github.com/mims-harvard/MedTok), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04397)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-40 · DiPro (NeurIPS 2025) · To be claimed

Implement DiPro for longitudinal EHR and sequential chest X-ray disease-progression modeling on MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR. [code](https://github.com/Chenliu-svg/DiPro), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11112)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-41 · HeartLang (ICLR 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the HeartLang ECG language model and PTB-XL, CPSC2018, and Chapman ECG classification benchmarks, coordinating with PTB-XL loader PRs #1187 and #1323. [code](https://github.com/PKUDigitalHealth/HeartLang), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10707)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-42 · APN Irregular Time-Series Forecasting (AAAI 2025) · To be claimed

Add APN as a simple baseline model alongside an irregular clinical time-series forecasting task on PhysioNet 2012 and MIMIC. [code](https://github.com/decisionintelligence/APN), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11250)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-43 · ARMR (IJCAI 2025) · To be claimed

Implement ARMR (Adaptively Responsive Network) for PyHealth's MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV medication-recommendation tasks. [code](https://github.com/seucoin/armr2), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04428)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-44 · DearLLM (AAAI 2025) · To be claimed

Implement DearLLM, which uses LLM-deduced feature correlations as a graph prior, on PyHealth's MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV prediction tasks. [code](https://github.com/Artessay/DearLLM), [paper](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v39i1.32079)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-46 · GAME Multi-Institution Code Embeddings (Nature Communications 2025) · To be claimed

Add GAME harmonized medical code embeddings as a drop-in embedding initializer for PyHealth models on MIMIC-IV and OMOP. [code](https://github.com/celehs/GAME), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08547)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-47 · II-KEA (EMNLP 2025) · To be claimed

Implement II-KEA, a knowledge-enhanced agentic causal-discovery diagnosis predictor, for PyHealth's MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV tasks. [code](https://github.com/hanxiaoxue114/II-KEA_HealthcareAgent), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16288)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-49 · Joint Sequence and Image Irregular Time-Series Model (AAAI 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the self-supervised joint sequence-and-image model for irregular medical time series on PhysioNet 2012 and PhysioNet 2019 sepsis tasks. [code](https://github.com/zju-d3/AAAI25-Irregular-Medical-Time-Series), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.06134)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-50 · UDC Rare-Disease Prediction (WWW 2025) · To be claimed

Implement UDC (Unveiling Discrete Clues) for rare-disease prediction on MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU. [code](https://github.com/Data-Designer/UDCHealth)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-51 · Diffmv Missing-View Diffusion (KDD 2025) · To be claimed

Implement Diffmv, a unified diffusion framework for multimodal EHR prediction with random missing views and view laziness on MIMIC-III/IV and eICU. [code](https://github.com/xmed-lab/MMHealth), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16373)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-52 · APRICOT-M (Nature Communications 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the APRICOT-M state-space model and real-time ICU acuity and therapy-requirement prediction tasks on eICU and MIMIC-IV. [code](https://github.com/iheallab/apricotM), [paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62121-1)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-53 · KnowRare (npj Digital Medicine 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the KnowRare domain-adaptation model and rare-condition ICU outcome tasks across MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU. [code](https://github.com/JasonZuu/KnowRare), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06432)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-54 · LLMs as EHR Encoders (npj Digital Medicine 2025) · To be claimed

Add the LLM-embedding EHR encoder baseline (serialize EHR events, embed with an LLM, and fit a linear head) on EHRSHOT and MIMIC tasks. [code](https://github.com/stefanhgm/ehrshot-benchmark), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17403)

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-55 · MEME Pseudo-Notes EHR Model (npj Digital Medicine 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the MEME multiple-embedding model (EHR-to-pseudo-notes) and MIMIC-IV-ED disposition and decompensation tasks on MIMIC-IV and EHRSHOT. [code](https://github.com/Simonlee711/MEME), [paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-025-01777-x)

#### ▲ · BTY-22 · VAE PyHealth 2.0 Migration · To be claimed

Port pyhealth/models/vae.py to the PyHealth 2.0 BaseModel and SampleDataset API so it trains through the standard Trainer, with unit tests and an example notebook. [code](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/master/pyhealth/models/vae.py)

#### ▲ · BTY-57 · ProtoECGNet (MLHC 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the ProtoECGNet prototype-based ECG classifier and PTB-XL multi-label classification task, coordinating with open PR #1323. [code](https://github.com/bbj-lab/protoecgnet), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08713)

#### ▲ · BTY-58 · ETHOS-ARES (GigaScience 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the ETHOS generative timeline model and MEDS-based hospital outcome tasks (mortality, ICU admission, readmission, and length of stay) on MIMIC-IV using PyHealth's MEDSDataset. [code](https://github.com/ipolharvard/ethos-ares), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.06124)

#### ▲ · BTY-59 · MedPatch (MLHC 2025) · To be claimed

Implement MedPatch confidence-guided multimodal fusion (EHR time series, CXR, and notes) on MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR alongside MedFuse. [code](https://github.com/nyuad-cai/MedPatch), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.09182)

#### ▲ · BTY-60 · TrajSurv (MLHC 2025) · To be claimed

Implement the TrajSurv continuous-trajectory survival model and survival prediction tasks on MIMIC-III and eICU. [code](https://github.com/zengsihang/TrajSurv), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00657)

#### ▲ · BTY-61 · MultimodalMIMIC (ICML 2023) · To be claimed

Add the irregular multimodal EHR model (time attention over irregularly sampled vitals/labs fused with clinical notes) for MIMIC-III in-hospital mortality and phenotyping. [code](https://github.com/XZhang97666/MultimodalMIMIC)

#### ▲ · BTY-63 · MIU-VL Medical Image VLMs (ICLR 2023) · To be claimed

Add prompt-based pretrained vision-language model baselines for medical image detection in PyHealth. [code](https://github.com/MembrAI/MIU-VL)

#### ━ · BTY-65 · CHET Dynamic Disease Graphs (AAAI 2022) · To be claimed

Implement CHET (transition functions over dynamic disease graphs) for diagnosis and heart-failure prediction on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV. [code](https://github.com/luchang-cs/chet)

#### ━ · BTY-67 · CEHR-GPT (arXiv 2024) · To be claimed

Implement the CEHR-GPT generative OMOP foundation model for synthetic patient timelines, building on PyHealth's existing CEHR embeddings and processor. [code](https://github.com/knatarajan-lab/cehrgpt), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04400)

#### ━ · BTY-68 · DescEmb Text-Based Code Embedding (MLHC 2022) · To be claimed

Implement DescEmb to embed medical codes from their text descriptions so a single model transfers across coding systems on MIMIC-III and eICU. [code](https://github.com/hoon9405/DescEmb)

#### ━ · BTY-69 · HiCu Curriculum ICD Coding (MLHC 2022) · To be claimed

Add HiCu curriculum learning over the ICD hierarchy to PyHealth's automated medical-coding task on MIMIC-III clinical notes. [code](https://github.com/wren93/HiCu-ICD)

#### ▼ · BTY-70 · GenoML Multimodal Parkinson's Classifier (npj Parkinson's Disease 2022) · To be claimed

Add the multimodal (genetics and clinical) Parkinson's disease classifier in PyHealth, noting that PPMI data access and a loader are required. [code](https://github.com/GenoML/GenoML_multimodal_PD)

#### ▼ · BTY-71 · Convolution Over Medical Entities (AI in Medicine 2021) · To be claimed

Implement the multimodal CNN over extracted medical entities combined with clinical time series for MIMIC-III mortality and length-of-stay prediction. [code](https://github.com/tanlab/ConvolutionMedicalNer)

#### ▼ · BTY-75 · BiteNet (ICDM 2020) · To be claimed

Implement BiteNet (Bidirectional Temporal Encoder Network) for diagnosis and readmission prediction on MIMIC-III. [code](https://github.com/Xueping/BiteNet)

#### ▼ · BTY-76 · Clinical Fusion Structured + Notes Baselines (BMC MIDM 2020) · To be claimed

Add the structured-plus-unstructured clinical notes fusion baselines for MIMIC-III mortality, length of stay, and readmission prediction. [code](https://github.com/onlyzdd/clinical-fusion)

## Claimed

### Dataset

#### ⏫︎ · BTY-23 · SHHS Dataset PyHealth 2.0 Migration · Claimed by @ptsoumaki through #1500

Move SHHSDataset off the legacy BaseSignalDataset onto the 2.0 BaseDataset (YAML config and processors) and ensure the sleep-staging task runs on it, using TUEV as the reference port. [code1](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/master/pyhealth/datasets/shhs.py), [code2](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/master/pyhealth/datasets/tuev.py)

### Model

#### ▲ · BTY-21 · GAN PyHealth 2.0 Migration · Claimed by @margaretdu through #1303

Port pyhealth/models/gan.py to the PyHealth 2.0 BaseModel and SampleDataset API with unit tests and an example notebook. Coordinate with open PR #1303, which adds a MIMIC-III code-set mode. [code](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/master/pyhealth/models/gan.py)

#### ▲ · BTY-64 · SleepKD Sleep EEG Distillation (IJCAI 2023) · Claimed by @samehaisaa through #1503, @irvifa through #1518

Add SleepKD teacher-assistant knowledge distillation for single-channel sleep EEG staging on PyHealth's Sleep-EDF and ISRUC sleep-staging tasks. [code](https://github.com/HychaoWang/SleepKD)

#### ▼ · BTY-72 · Temporal Pointwise Convolution / TPC (CHIL 2021) · Claimed by @SubbuM123 through #1412, @tkumar007 through #1428

Implement the Temporal Pointwise Convolution (TPC) model for ICU length-of-stay and mortality prediction on eICU and MIMIC-IV. [code](https://github.com/EmmaRocheteau/TPC-LoS-prediction)

#### ▼ · BTY-74 · BEHRT (Scientific Reports 2020) · Claimed by @Alhibb through #1517

Implement BEHRT (BERT with age and visit-segment embeddings and masked-code pretraining) for next-visit diagnosis prediction on MIMIC. [code](https://github.com/deepmedicine/BEHRT/tree/master)

### Interpretability

#### ▲ · BTY-25 · Grad-CAM Interpretability Method · Claimed by @irvifa through #1499

Add a Grad-CAM interpreter to pyhealth.interpret for CNN-based signal and image models (including a 2.0 CNN signal baseline if needed), matching the interface of existing methods such as chefer.py. [code1](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/tree/master/pyhealth/interpret), [code2](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/blob/master/pyhealth/interpret/methods/chefer.py), [link](https://github.com/jacobgil/pytorch-grad-cam)

#### ▲ · BTY-26 · Raw Attention Interpretability Method · Claimed by @irvifa through #1496

Add raw attention weights as a baseline attribution method for PyHealth's Transformer so it can be compared against attention rollout and Chefer relevance. [code](https://github.com/sunlabuiuc/PyHealth/tree/master/pyhealth/interpret), [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.09838)

### Calibration

#### ━ · BTY-66 · Fair Conformal Predictors for Medical Imaging (AAAI 2022) · Claimed by @Alhibb through #1513

Add group-conditional (fair) conformal prediction sets to pyhealth.calib and demonstrate them on an existing PyHealth medical imaging dataset. [code](https://github.com/clu5/AAAI-22)

raw.title: Mission 01 — Exchange — Season II

labels.name: source:h2
labels.description: Demand exposed by Telegraph Hackathon Season II

raw.body:
**Start with the customer and work backwards.** This mission is about delivering something useful, not accumulating disconnected Intents or registrations. A contributor can build the whole solution—application, intelligence Provider and relevant evaluation work—or concentrate on one part and work with others. All three hackathon tracks are open, with separate qualifying entries under the [official rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules).

## The opportunity

**Who it serves:** Exchange listings, surveillance and counterparty-risk desks.

**Problem:** Token listing, market-integrity and counterparty reviews are slow, opaque or priced per seat. The buyer needs a defensible decision with verifiable inputs and a cost line.

**A useful result:** A signed or tamper-evident listing, surveillance or counterparty memo with the input evidence, receipts and cost of reaching the decision.

Pick a specific customer and workflow. Establish the alternative they use today, a realistic willingness-to-pay or budget constraint, a measurable result, acceptable error and response time. These are example opportunities, not exclusive products or confirmed customers. See [Exchange](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions/exchange) and the [full mission catalogue](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions).

| Route | Actual outcome to build | Shared capability families to investigate and use |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Autonomous listing review** | Take a candidate contract and treasury wallet, obtain the relevant audit, on-chain, sanctions and authenticity intelligence, and output a LIST / REVIEW / REJECT memo explaining every finding. | `SMART_CONTRACT_AUDIT`, `ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY`, `SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH`, `SOCIAL_BOT_DETECTION`, `CODE_REVIEW` |
| **2. Market integrity alert feed** | Monitor a market for suspicious trading and liquidity anomalies; produce actionable ranked alerts and optionally expose the alert feed through a Miner. | `WASH_TRADING_DETECTION`, `LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY` |
| **3. Counterparty solvency handshake** | Two simulated counterparties buy independently verifiable attestations and make a credit decision without sharing confidential books. | `ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION`, `ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY`, `CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY` |

**First milestone:** one realistic input → a paid Telegraph intelligence request → a checked result with its source/uncertainty → a useful action or answer → receipt and total cost. Include one failure case before expanding the workflow. You do **not** need to implement all three example products.

**Tests worth demonstrating:** Use one legitimate and one deliberately risky token fixture; test an unavailable block, conflicting sources and a rejected/uncertain screening. Never label an unsupported risk result as safe.

**Measures that matter:** Decision cost per token, latency, false clearance rate, proportion of findings backed by traceable evidence.

## Intelligence needed

**Published starting families:** `SMART_CONTRACT_AUDIT`, `SECURITY_REVIEW`, `ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY`, `TOKEN_TOTAL_SUPPLY_VERIFY`, `SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH`, `SOCIAL_BOT_DETECTION`, `WASH_TRADING_DETECTION`, `LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY`.

These are shared network capabilities, **not separate bounties** created for this mission. The same capability may support several missions, with one canonical Intent, one Provider market and one evaluation pool. The list is a starting map, not a mandatory bill of materials or proof of live coverage.

Before implementing anything, inspect the [live canonical Intent list](https://devnode.telegraphprotocol.com/engine/v1/intents), [request and response schemas](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema), [ranked Providers](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/explore) and [published Intent catalogue](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/INTENTS.md). Use the **exact** live `intent_name` and `request.params`; family names and guessed `_GENERAL` suffixes are not reliable request identifiers. Some unknown names return HTTP 200 with a null schema, which is not a working Intent. The [mission mapping](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/MISSIONS.md) is helpful for discovery, but the node determines which capabilities are callable and what evaluation path applies.

A finished report, dashboard, refund, memo or decision is usually **application composition**, not a new protocol Intent. Use existing reusable capabilities first. Only propose a new Intent for genuinely reusable intelligence missing from the catalogue.

## Ways to contribute

### Apps & Agents — deliver the product

Build a runnable application that **autonomously purchases or sells intelligence through Telegraph** and uses the response to complete a meaningful task. Start with the smallest useful customer workflow; confirm the supporting Intents and live Provider quality before committing to an architecture.

Choose the right [delivery path](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/inference-paths): [Engine Ask](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/engine-ask) for fresh on-demand work; [x402](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/x402-inference) or [escrow](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/escrow-inference) for supported settlement; [WebSocket Signals](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/websocket-signals) when reusable streamed intelligence is appropriate; [MCP](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/mcp-server) for integrations. A Signal subscription is not a substitute for a fresh, user-specific check. A 402 payment challenge is not evidence of a completed purchase.

Make uncertainty visible. Handle partial or conflicting answers, stale data, missing Providers, spending limits and failures. Prove the total **cost per useful completed outcome** rather than multiplying paid requests unnecessarily. Reuse valid fresh intelligence when permitted; avoid paying repeatedly for the same shared fact. Irreversible transactions and sensitive actions require the user's authorization. Simulated or testnet behavior must be labelled as such.

**Completion evidence:** runnable app and instructions, a new realistic input producing a useful result, authentic Telegraph request/payment evidence, costs and latency, and a reproducible failure case. A static interface or a Miner registration alone does not qualify as the app.

### Miners / Providers — supply the intelligence

Identify a missing or weak capability for this customer workflow. Test existing Providers to understand the quality bar. Independent competing implementations for the same canonical Intent are welcome; show how yours performs in accuracy, coverage, freshness, price, reliability or latency. Implement a callable service for a supported canonical Intent, following its actual request/response schema and [Miner YAML guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/yaml-config).

Check the [validation guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/validation-api) and current [registration steps](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/miner-registration). **Known documentation limitation (Nov 15):** the guide says its `POST /dashboard/validate` endpoint currently returns 404; use the available web checks, documented local checks and supported registration dry-run instead of treating that POST as working. Use the [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet) for eligible testnet needs. Confirm the registration is active and the service answers the actual Intent; capture its registration ID, test cases, measured results and paid request evidence. Distinguish direct diagnostic requests from selection by ranked routing.

Share working endpoints and registration IDs here so other applications and missions can reuse the Provider.

### Evaluators — measure whether the intelligence is good

Use the selected Intent's **actual node class, family and scoring path**, not the name or an old bounty description, to determine what's needed:

- **Deterministic:** reliable public truth-source material and the supported comparator path. A new judgment adapter is not inherently required.
- **Hybrid:** the checkable truth source/comparator and judgment contribution that the live scoring path actually uses.
- **Judgment:** sourced, balanced better/worse examples and a compatible evaluation adapter **where needed**. Do not assume every Intent needs a new adapter plus material.

Contribute through [Anjoman Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval), following [material formats and provenance](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/contribute-evaluation-data) and the [scoring-module guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/build-a-scoring-module) when applicable. Use primary evidence, timestamps, block/chain or jurisdiction identifiers, correct units and tolerances. Include correct, incorrect, incomplete and ambiguous cases; avoid datasets solvable merely by answer length, keywords or copied prompt wording. Test on unseen sources and failure types. Confirm **eligible / rejected** material state and actual module status separately; passing a local test or uploading rows does not imply canonical promotion.

A single project may contribute a working app, a Provider and genuinely useful evaluation work. Each track still requires its own qualifying evidence. No extra or duplicative component is needed simply to claim participation across all three.

## Share work here as it happens

**Read the latest comments and existing [Bounties Issues](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/issues) to understand current activity, available capabilities and opportunities to collaborate.** Multiple contributors are welcome to independently build applications, Providers and Evaluators for the same mission or Intent, including competing implementations. Existing work does not reserve a mission, product or Intent. Share progress and findings so others can collaborate, reuse useful contributions or compete independently.

If using the existing Bounties workflow, post `/claim` and then a short comment identifying your scope. Claims are **non-exclusive**. Keep the thread current with `/progress <update>` at least every **72 hours** while claimed, and link relevant work from other mission threads. Useful updates include:

```text
Scope: [product or capability + customer problem]
Track(s): [Apps & Agents / Miners / Providers / Evaluators]
Working on: [concrete deliverable, canonical Intents if known]
Reusing (optional): [existing work, Providers, evaluations + links]
Approach: [what you are building and how you plan to deliver it]
Current state: [building / tested / blocked / submitted]
Proof or next milestone: [repo/demo/endpoint, reproducible result]
```

When ready, post `/submit <links and evidence>` for your individual contribution, **and** use the official Anjoman submission path. GitHub comments coordinate work; they are not the final hackathon entry or evaluation upload. One team's submission does not close the mission to other participants. Existing accepted contributions and claims remain valid; reviewers assess individual entries separately. Don't post credentials, private customer data, protected evaluation samples or sensitive exploit details.

## Prove it, share it, submit it

A strong entry can be tested by someone outside the team: provide a live demo or callable endpoint, public-safe repository, run instructions, real request IDs/receipts, one failure test, honest cost figures and limitations. For apps, explain what was purchased and **what useful action happened afterward**. Consider listing working apps in [Anjoman Apps](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/apps) for others to discover.

The [Season II judging rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules) apply across all three tracks (100 points each; **70/100** overall and each track's stated technical minimum). Apps are scored on technical quality/mainnet readiness (35 points, minimum 24), commercial viability (25), independent adoption (10), integration and usage (5), reproducibility (5), and organic growth/developer activation (20). Providers and Evaluators have their **own** track rubrics on the same rules page.

The 20 growth points cover **useful education (5), ease of adoption (5), organic distribution (5), and independent community activation (5)**. Share a working explanation or video, a genuinely useful walkthrough, and **at least three meaningful original progress updates on separate dates**. Invite independent developers to try, reproduce or integrate your work; show their real feedback and results. Publish where relevant (GitHub, Discord, X, technical communities) and follow the published tagging/link guidance. Bought engagement, fake traffic, manipulated stars, self-dealing and fabricated demand do not count. **Star the [Bounties repository](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties)** as required in Section 5; this is an entry requirement, not proof of growth.

**Prizes and possible earnings:** $7,000 for the Season II main competition ($3,000 Apps, $2,000 Providers, $2,000 Evaluators), plus $3,000 reserved for separate December challenges—not an extra automatic Season II pool. Awards depend on eligibility and verification. Beyond prizes, eligible Providers may earn from paid usage, Evaluator contributions may earn applicable protocol rewards, and products may generate revenue if customers adopt them. **Nothing is guaranteed** by a claim, registration or testnet call. This is a coordination Issue, not a separately funded GitHub bounty.

**Deadline:** **December 1, 2026, 23:59 UTC** for the main competition; **November 20** is the progress showcase. Finish the [official H2 submission](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon) using its live form when available, selecting the tracks and attaching distinct evidence for each. As of November 15, the site says the final form opens later; don't mistake a GitHub `/submit` comment for the final submission. The official rules control eligibility, awards, dates and any subsequent announcements.

## Before reporting a blocker

| Problem | Check first |
|---|---|
| Intent request fails or returns an empty schema | Select an exact live canonical Intent; inspect `request.params`, response fields and active Provider coverage in the [schema guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema). A 200 response with `request: null` is not a valid Intent. |
| No result after x402 or escrow | Follow the documented full payment flow; a 402 offer alone is not a settled purchase. Check available receipt and account evidence. |
| A Miner looks highly ranked but answers the wrong question | Reproduce the input, preserve the raw/shaped result and actual receipt, compare with a direct diagnostic call, and report the specific ranking gap. |
| Registration, validation or bond trouble | Check the registration and validation docs, live node state, chain configuration and [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet); the documented `POST /dashboard/validate` route is currently flagged as broken. |
| Evaluation material or module rejected | Check eligible/rejected reasons, provenance, required shape, supported family kind and public scoring requirements; don't infer adapter requirements from an Intent's label. |
| A similar app or capability already exists | Independent competing implementations are welcome. Review existing work for useful references, reuse or collaborate where appropriate, or proceed independently. No exclusive claims. |

For a genuine unresolved protocol defect, post a concise reproducible report here (exact Intent, public request, expected/actual behavior and safe evidence), then use [Discord](https://discord.gg/telegraphprotocol) for escalation if necessary.

## Done when

- [ ] A real customer need and runnable app/agent that solves it are demonstrated.
- [ ] A supported paid Telegraph request/sale leads to a useful action, with authentic receipt/accounting evidence.
- [ ] Relevant shared Intents have usable Provider supply and evaluation coverage, or precisely documented remaining gaps.
- [ ] A reviewer can reproduce a realistic success and failure case, including total cost and latency.
- [ ] Contributors' progress and relevant final entries are linked in comments; evidence distinguishes testnet, production and genuine external adoption.

This checklist measures **mission coverage**, not one person's prize eligibility. A successful app does not imply every possible workflow or every mapped Intent is complete. Keep this Issue available for distinct contributors; do not close it merely because one scope finished.

## Reward

**No standalone GitHub payout.** Season II prizes and ongoing protocol earnings are separate and governed by their published eligibility and payment terms.

raw.body:
Capture for Front, matching what `packages/zendesk-app` does in Zendesk: record what the AI drafted, what the human sent, and one-line reason, from inside the tool the expert already works in.

**Bounty: $150**, paid on merge (PayPal, Wise or GitHub Sponsors — your choice).

### What it should do

A Front plugin that, for a conversation with an AI draft in the composer:

1. Detects a draft landing in the reply box and shows `Draft inserted · N words`.
2. Offers the reason picker (`reason_pack`, same eight codes as the claims pack; `support` pack also supported) with an optional note.
3. On send, `POST /v1/capture` with `source: "front"`, `externalId: "fr:<conversation id>"`, the conversation as `context`, and `draft` / `sent` as `{ text, fields? }`.
4. Honours `require_reason`: a changed reply is blocked until there is a reason.
5. Never blocks the send — a failed capture logs and gets out of the way.

### Shape to follow

- `packages/zendesk-app/src/capture.ts` and its test are the reference; the capture payload is documented in [docs/capture.md](docs/capture.md).
- Land it as `packages/front-plugin`, same build setup (`tsup`, `pnpm --filter` scripts, a `dist/*.zip` from `scripts/package.mjs`).
- Front's plugin API: https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/plugin-sdk
- TypeScript strict, no `any`. Unit tests for the payload builder are required; a live Front account is not (mock the SDK surface the way the Zendesk tests mock the ZAF client).

### Out of scope

Front's own analytics, per-agent rates, anything that reads a conversation with no draft in it. Capture reads a conversation only after a draft appears.

Questions: comment here or shireen@overturn.run. Say in a comment that you are picking it up so two people don't build it twice.

raw.body:
> **D1 reassessed gate: GO to bounded DESIGN ONLY**, following accepted PR #1305 at `24f26efabdd26011374a84accedef986717d9a31`. [Reassessment, seven portability fields and independent PASS](https://github.com/m0smith/genia-2026/issues/1250#issuecomment-6550211564). B1 is resolved; no remaining semantic blocker for design. No RED/implementation authorization, ordinary linking, Slice E or R29. The original preflight remains historical evidence; its B1-only NO-GO is superseded by this reassessment.

**Classification:** Follow-up / required semantic foundation, unnumbered after R20/#1067 and before R29 implementation. **Status:** Approved Model B contract; Python Slices A/B/C merged. Slice D ordinary cross-module linking and Slice E closed-function publication remain unimplemented. Parent remains open. **Authority:** GENIA_STATE.md, GENIA_RULES.md, GENIA_REPL_README.md, README.md. **Strategy:** docs/strategy/killer-workflow.md, docs/strategy/release-roadmap.md, docs/strategy/roadmap/sequence.md. **Process:** AGENTS.md, docs/process/run-change.md, docs/process/08-roadmap-ticketing.md.

**Original problem (historical intake):** R20 required explicit `open` and ordinary functions were closed by default. The approved follow-up reverses default openness and introduces `=:` bindings/closed declarations. Python now executes immutable bindings and local ordinary default-open functions; closed forms only parse/lower and ordinary cross-module linking remains absent. #1067 explicitly excluded these changes; do not reclassify completed #1067 work or overwrite historical contract. New Sheet/Flow/extension work may otherwise depend on a soon-to-change function model.

**Non-goals:** no implementation authority from ticket/roadmap text, no implicit cross-module modification, no change to R20 dispatch precedence unless separately justified, no new annotation or `@closed` syntax, no broad Core IR versioning (R41 boundary), no R28 reopen, no unrelated cleanup. Preserve #1230 temporary fallback retirement gate separately. Existing behavior remains authoritative until merged, tested, and reflected in STATE.

**Drift controls:** docs only claim implemented behavior after actual landing; no silent Python/C++ parity claims; preserve explicit module extension authority and protected values / Outcome / Flow semantics; compare breaking source compatibility and migration costs.

**Dependency:** #1249 contract is approved by #1255. A/B/C are delivered in Python; D and E depend on B/C. Local E does not require D, but combined D+E targeting/publication checks belong to #1251. R29 waits for requisite acceptance or an explicitly approved bounded deferral; none is approved by this planning task.

**Scope includes (subject to approved contract):** grammar/parser/Core IR non-breaking carriers; lexical immutable binding write/redeclaration diagnostics; open-by-default ordinary definitions; closed `=:` function grouped-clause construction; mixing/ambiguity diagnostics; authorized cross-module contributions; function identity/closure/reflection considerations. Split implementation into independently mergeable semantic slices if one process run is too broad.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Contract-linked failing shared spec tests before implementation; commit/red-test evidence retained.
- [ ] Positive and negative specs for immutable rebinding, nested scope/shadowing, parameters, closures, function clause grouping/mixing, import/extend/use, accidental cross-module extension, duplicate/ambiguous dispatch, recursion/TCO, module isolation.
- [ ] Python reference host implementation matches approved contract; C++ supported capability behavior has verified conformance, or precise issue-backed capability gap documented.
- [ ] Existing R20 functionality and killer-workflow pipeline regressions preserved except explicitly approved breaking deltas; migration impact recorded.
- [ ] Changed public/internal code carries maintained documentation; synchronization plan for STATE/RULES/REPL README/README, semantic facts and MCP language profile.

**Excludes:** release-wide audit, broad IR versioning, opportunistic module privacy redesign, unrelated R29 features. **Risk:** high. **Phases:** contract prerequisite → design → failing tests → minimal implementation → focused docs sync → focused audit evidence. Do not declare completed until verified.

## Live progress / selected next preflight (2026-10-30)

[Foundation decision and complete D1 scope/acceptance/evidence plan](https://github.com/m0smith/genia-2026/issues/1251#issuecomment-6535802813), inspected at main `def3860858e9bf066ffe5931d1cd820c51bd2e87`.

| Slice | Actual status |
|---|---|
| A parser/Core IR | Python #1260 merged cf384030a6ce1746b82ac2b6c291d2a598c24756; C++ required syntax/lowering gap remains [genia-cpp#50](https://github.com/m0smith/genia-cpp/issues/50). |

| C local ordinary functions | Python #1270 merged09804b565a30c2995a7d045d74faf8e880994ff4; #1302 docs/#1304 transport merged; #1299 independently accepted/closed. C++ default-open remains unsupported. |

| E closed publication | Not implemented: whole-group validation, initializing/committed/failed identity, synchronous annotation self-call admission, immutable self/defining name, failed-value safety and use/introspection ordering remain. |

### Next task: D1 — module-completion projections (PREFLIGHT ONLY)

Classification: bounded pre-R29 foundation follow-up under this existing issue; no new child ticket (portable design §9). Owner: m0smith / authority implementation maintainer. Risk: high metadata/ownership drift; future implementation needs full applicable process.

Capture, after original base module initializes successfully and before completed-cache publication, exported ordinary-base ordered clause records/provenance plus independent defining-binding annotations, effective doc and effective shared help/summary. Re-exports reuse the original completed projection. Preserve live C callable aliases; freeze structure without deep-freezing Ref/Cell payloads. Use host-local assertions for snapshot properties unobservable before D2; source/direct-IR and existing shared R16 import-inertness/ordinary/metadata/explicit-R20 regressions establish preserved public behavior. Internal tests cannot stand in for D2's later shared observable linking RED. Report actual Python/C++ applicability and exact issue-backed gaps; required syntax remains required. No new capability solely for internal machinery. The eventual implementation must satisfy all required CI/review/portability/docs gates, without weakening coverage.

**Phase boundary:** preflight → bounded design/readiness review → separately authorized committed RED → implementation citing RED → maintainability review → truthful per-slice docs/MCP impact assessment → independent behavioral/truth audit → distillation/required CI. This task selects preflight; it does not authorize RED or code.

Seven historical Python TIMEOUTs retain failed outcomes/provenance; the linked decision recommends acceptable historical uncertainty without additional retrospective experiments now, not proven cause or future-gate waiver. #1251 remains open and R29 remains NO-GO.
