raw.title: NapAttack Codex coordination: four chats, task ownership and Claude handoffs
raw.body:
<!-- MYGAME_LEAD_BOARD_LINK -->
**Current coordination:** [MyGame Codex · lead task board](https://github.com/rempemat-eng/appify/issues/149#issuecomment-6475643125) (edited in place).

Matt asked this chat to coordinate the four new Codex chats with Claude through GitHub.

This is the live registration and handoff thread. The durable handoff is in [draft PR #150](https://github.com/rempemat-eng/appify/pull/150), with an additive AGENTS.md pointer once Claude merges it. AGENTS.md and docs/vision/coherence-plan.md remain the authority for scope and ownership. Existing explicit per-chat assignments and start conditions are preserved. No game rules or mechanics are approved here.

## Four chat assignments

The current continuation records clarify the groupings below. These are assigned scopes, not proof that a worker has acknowledged this hub or is running.

| Chat / assigned scope | Order and branches | Start / integration gates | Acknowledged here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NapAttack Codex · C29 C30 world canvas | C29 on `codex/world-saves`, then C30 on `codex/ways-route-graph` | Both #123 and #126 changes must be on main before implementation. C30 also consumes #118's ways contract. | Not yet |
| NapAttack Codex · C32 C31 gates and map | C32 on `codex/ci-gates`, then C31 on `codex/world-map-canvas` | Both #142 and #145 changes must be on main before either implementation. C31 additionally needs the canvas and C29 save contracts. | Not yet |
| C33 economy simulation | One simulation-only PR; reuse an existing branch if present | Model current rules and label L2/G10 as scenarios. #143 remains a proposal, not production rules. | Not yet |
| C34 native pixels | One isolated spike PR; reuse an existing branch if present | Agree platform-adapter ownership with Claude A, consume the canvas contract, keep the flag off; memory/frame-time results require an actual native dev build. | Not yet |

C29/C30 and C32/C31 must honour their explicit no-implementation-before-prerequisites instructions. While blocked, use read-only review; do not write speculative production adapters or take another chat's tasks.

## Register an existing chat

Post one comment with `ACK | task=Cn (and next task) | chat=<existing title> | branch=<existing task branch> | PR=<link/status> | files=<owned paths> | based-on=<main SHA> | state=<state> | needs=<dependency>`.

Read the latest comments, main, queue/Feedback and open PRs before editing. Existing claims win. Do not steal a task after an elapsed timer or push to another worker's branch. If duplicate claims appear, stop overlapping writes and resolve them here with Claude A.

## File boundaries and known blockers

- C29 alone owns save-schema/serialization changes and shared historical save fixtures. C31 supplies its discovery payload and migration requirements to C29. Claude A retains `lib/world-layouts.ts`, `lib/world-save.ts`, generated canvas files, world traversal and renderer files.
- C30 owns new pure gating/tests, not the generated graph or visual/traversal implementation. In #126, the current graph is per-region, and direct window walking searches can bypass graph fallback. Test all search paths, future connectors/transport edges, cached routes and cancellation; graph-edge removal alone is insufficient.
- C32 owns CI wiring and summaries. The new whole-world command is `check:world-audit`; preserve existing `check:world` save checks. #142's redraw/measurement/kit-marker prerequisites still apply. Hash-based preview caches must not skip compliance checks.
- Coordinate additive `package.json` edits before writing; keep dependency changes and lockfiles under one owner at a time. C34 adds packages only through `npx expo install`.
- Canvas draft origins are placeholders. Migrate against versioned historical transforms, never whatever origin the current generator produces.
- #126 also has an unresolved retained-tile-budget review comment. Do not call skipped checks passes or enable WORLD_CANVAS on the strength of source tests.
- C33 cannot change live payouts, costs, save data or balances. Do not fold the separate #146 home-base proposal into C33 without a new instruction.
- C34 cannot edit Claude's components or claim desktop results as native/device evidence. A report-only spike remains incomplete if the native measurement requirement is not met.

## Persistent automatic assignment checks

On 20 October, Matt explicitly requested that ALL FOUR slots activate after receiving tasks from this coordinator or Claude. Four persistent hourly continuations are now enabled and their saved prompts/schedules have been read back:

| Slot | Initial work | Automatic check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `world-canvas` | C29 → C30 | Hourly; rechecks #123/#126 on main and C30's additional contracts before implementation |
| `ci-map` | C32 → C31 | Hourly; rechecks #142/#145 and the current marker/canvas/save requirements |
| `economy` | C33 | Hourly; preserves the existing PR #151 worker and looks for addressed follow-ups |
| `native-pixels` | C34 | Hourly; preserves codex/native-pixels and consumes Claude A's agreed pixel-image boundary |

The earlier C29/C30 merge-only watcher is paused after its hourly replacement was confirmed enabled. There are four active NapAttack assignment continuations, not an extra competing merge watcher.

The checks remain enabled after the initial tasks finish. They must not pause merely because they have no work, recreate completed tasks, start arbitrary generic queue work, or create restart chains. They report only meaningful changes. Explicit PAUSED/CANCELLED/REASSIGNED instructions are honoured.

### Assign a future task

Claude A or the coordinator can post an explicit assignment here, or in the current queue/Feedback, with:

`ASSIGN | slot=world-canvas/ci-map/economy/native-pixels | task=<stable task ID and revision> | scope=<approved work> | prerequisites=<real gates> | branch=<own isolated branch> | files=<agreed ownership>`

Choose one actual slot value, not the whole list. Each checker reads the issue AND comments, the latest main/AGENTS/coordination/vision files and its task PR. It records the assignment ID and actual branch/head, so later checks know what was acknowledged, completed, released, paused or reassigned. New assignments remain within Matt's approved project scope and lane boundaries.

An active owner's branch is not taken over because it looks quiet or a lease expires. If ownership is unconfirmed, the checker performs read-only review and requests a handoff once. Shared saves/manifests remain single-writer work.

Claude A has now acknowledged this hub and supplied integration decisions in his comment; workers must read those decisions rather than treat them as unanswered.

These are saved-task continuations, not remote control of arbitrary existing chat windows. The enabled settings have been verified; no real future hourly run or cross-chat delivery is claimed yet. Scheduling is not a guarantee of an exact execution time.

## Handoff and review

Each task gets its own draft PR, titled `[Cn taken] ...`. Keep it draft through iteration. Run `npm run verify` and `npm run check:art-repro` on the exact final source, mark ready once, then inspect matching CI. Only after matching CI passes use `[Cn complete]`. Do not repeatedly merge main just to refresh checks; follow current AGENTS.md's CI policy. Report failures/blocked dependencies accurately.

Each handoff records branch/head/base, files, what changed, tests/results, missing coverage and the precise request for the receiving chat or Claude. Feedback belongs on the existing task PR plus a short status here; Codex does not edit docs/vision to communicate unless Matt has explicitly authorised that narrow edit for the specific chat. The coordinator will use this issue and a docs/codex PR without extending that exception.

Claude A retains integration/merge responsibility under Matt's existing plan. Codex never pushes main, merges or enables auto-merge. Quiet activity is not a completion signal.

Claude A has acknowledged this hub. External Codex worker acknowledgements are tracked in the comments; do not infer receipt from a schedule setting. The coordinator cannot directly send into the four chat windows from this session. This is an asynchronous GitHub channel, not continuous supervision.

Ran: latest-main/AGENTS/queue/Feedback and PR/branch review; current continuation-assignment lookup; read-only canvas/ways/audit dependency review.
Did not test: full verify/art regeneration, browser gameplay, native builds/devices or worker implementations. No game source changed.

raw.body:
## Purpose
Keep **GridMates: Sudoku Beta 1** stable and make GitHub's canonical source, release metadata, and testing status unambiguous before additional significant features. The user has moved the separate Work chat to Word Search; this repository remains dedicated to Sudoku.

**Audit:** [November 16 repo health and safe-consolidation plan](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/blob/main/docs/SUDOKU_REPO_HEALTH_AND_BETA_STEWARDSHIP_2026-11-16.md)  
**Canonical Beta source:** [PR #42](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/pull/42) was merged to `main` in [commit `9256a5f`](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/commit/9256a5f239e232b9211aa5589a9e4383e96fea80); the published binary's recorded build source is `76cbfc1`.  
**Release evidence:** [v1 Beta 1 QA and artifact hashes](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/blob/main/docs/GRIDMATES_V1_BETA_RELEASE.md)  
**Owner-provided itch.io URL:** https://sir-spudacus.itch.io/gridmates-sudoku

### Beta 1.1 quality infrastructure (Nov 16, 2026)
- [x] [Core JVM CI PR #46](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/pull/46) merged to `main` as [`6ce8a44`](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/commit/6ce8a446997c492e13d6cb7890513fec10b38589). First [GitHub Actions run 43996910731](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/actions/runs/43996910731) **passed** (`:core:test`, ~1m 26s Gradle, no signing or Android build). 15-minute budget cap; path filters and concurrency cancellation preserve Actions minutes.
- [x] [Proof-invariant test PR #45](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/pull/45) merged to `main` as [`60e79b8`](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/commit/60e79b8de446a2347f09bb729701812de7d3724b), after [Actions run 43997216944](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/actions/runs/43997216944) **passed** the full core JVM test suite with the new seeded logic/Coach checks. These are sample-based regression tests, not definitive human-difficulty calibration.
- [x] [Versus UI PR #44](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/pull/44) merged to `main` as [`4cfe132`](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/commit/4cfe1321d554833fde39a9ec639d8955666bb433). Dedicated API 36 Android instrumentation [run 43999395717](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/actions/runs/43999395717) **passed 5/5 VersusPresenceUiTest cases (0 failed/skipped)** including the real-world emoji regression, large fonts, reconnect/result/rematch UI. Two earlier failed runs were **workflow setup/command errors**, corrected before this green run; neither reached the test assertions.
- [x] [PR #48](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/pull/48) merged as [`75a0a17`](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/commit/75a0a1784bc705a2714fa2e8d56146d4f0ab2018): safely clip 24-unit multiplayer names at emoji boundaries; test complete Versus winner state surviving a persisted room restart and the next race discarding the previous epoch. [Core GitHub Actions run 44001131055](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/actions/runs/44001131055) **passed** `:core:test`. No newly signed APK or actual two-device rematch test implied.
- [x] Prepared [Beta 1.1 owner-phone QA checklist](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/blob/main/docs/BETA_1_1_OWNER_PHONE_PLAYTEST.md), emphasizing original QA signer, install-over, saved games, two-phone Co-op/Versus/rematch, and no data clearing. **The checklist itself is not test evidence.**
- [ ] Verify updated Versus cards *visually on real phones* at normal and large system font scales, including emoji and two-line names, before signing off Beta 1.1 physical UX.
- [ ] Assemble/test a **new QA build only after** the approved Beta 1.1 UI fix and remaining relevant Android checks; protect the existing QA signer and app data. The published itch.io Beta 1 APK has not changed.

### Downloadable Beta 1.1 preview (Nov 17, 2026)
- [x] Delivered [isolated Sudoku Preview APK](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/actions/runs/44003023663) after successful core/Android unit/lint/build and app-ID/signature/SHA-256 checks. Source `15c14dde3611df2c67ad2c906ff2955856bec06e`; package `com.playereden.sudokutogether.qa.preview`; APK SHA-256 `579e95861da993e4320b2cdcced787c155702f2baa68894d1798815581a8b6e3`. The preview uses **new separate local data** and the original QA/public apps remain unchanged.
- [ ] Owner to install the preview on two phones and verify actual Solo/Daily/Coach, Co-op, Versus names/progress, match finish/rematch and Wi-Fi rejoin. These physical checks have **not** passed yet.
- [ ] Privately restore the **original** QA signing key as `SUDOKU_QA_KEYSTORE_BASE64` before any compatible QA install-over update. [Signed QA attempt](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/actions/runs/44002680103) stopped safely due to missing secret; do not replace the keystore or bypass signing checks.

### Release-confidence and update safety
- [x] **Owner-confirmed physical smoke check (Nov 16, 2026):** downloaded the public APK from itch.io, installed and launched it successfully; also installed and launched the QA build. This is an owner report, not an independent hash, signing, or device-matrix verification.
- [ ] Independently compare the actual itch-downloaded APK's **SHA-256, production signature, package ID and version** with the recorded release artifact before declaring artifact identity verified
- [ ] Test saved Solo/Daily, notes/Undo/Coach/Profile/Collection and restart; verify backup/restore without erasing QA data
- [ ] Recheck previously timed-out Android emulator paths on a healthy emulator or a real device; record which fail/reproduce versus environmental timeouts
- [x] **Owner screenshot evidence of a completed two-person Versus session (Nov 16):** one participant's device shows local/rival progress changing from 0/45 each to 4/45 versus 2/45; a later result screen correctly displays rival win 45/45 versus local 40/45, retains the local grid and offers host-started next race. This is **owner-provided screenshot evidence from the Beta 1 QA build**, not the public itch.io package; no independent APK hash or second-device capture is included.
- [ ] Complete **remaining current-build physical two-phone regression:** verify the finish notice on *both* phones, host actually starts a rematch, both join/continue, disconnect/reconnect, resumed rooms and old-save upgrade continuity; record phone/API and build on each device. Older Co-op owner reports do not establish this full sequence.
- [ ] Log source commit, APK hash, phone/API, observed result and known issues; don't label undocumented checks 'passed'

### Source, PR and documentation consolidation
- [x] Verify the exact head commits of staged PRs #33–#41 appear in merged PR #42's commit ancestry; no duplicate staged merge required. Broader behavior/code regression review remains in the release QA tasks above.
- [x] Owner approved source consolidation and PR #42 was merged into `main` with full history retained. **This does not mark every remaining physical QA gate completed.**
- [x] PR #33 recognized as merged; superseded draft PRs #34–#41 closed with source-ancestry traceability comments and no branch deletion. Historical QA branches/checkpoints preserved.
- [x] Updated README, CONTINUE_HERE, current handoff, delivery plan and dated audit to identify `main` as the current Beta source while retaining historical QA details.
- [x] Reconciled milestone issues [#10](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/issues/10)–[#14](https://github.com/PlayerEden/SudokuTogether/issues/14) against Beta 1 source and QA (Nov 16): each now distinguishes implemented features from deferred tests and future plans. All five issues **remain open** because their full original acceptance criteria are not yet evidenced.
- [ ] If desired, prepare tagged GitHub Release using **exact verified public artifact**, not a freshly re-signed download; retain production signing backup privately

### Later focused Sudoku polish (separate scoped issues)
- [ ] Reproduce player-reported UX bugs/accessibility and difficulty/hint issues on current Beta, one issue per verifiable problem
- [ ] Review Daily rewards, gift codes, expanded collections, share results and post-Versus comparison only after current beta stabilizes
- [ ] Keep internet matchmaking/cloud services a future, optional post-offline-launch effort

**Latest Beta 1.1 source readiness (November 16–17):** approved Beta 1 merge, redundant PR closure, core proof-invariant/emoji/room-recovery tests and focused API 36 Versus UI tests have passed their cited GitHub Actions runs. **No branches were deleted and no fresh QA/production APK, signer change, GitHub Release, public itch.io update or physical Beta 1.1 install-over was performed.** All remaining QA, release-integrity and device checks remain open.

raw.body:
<!-- V3_OWNER_CANONICAL_ENTRY_20261109 -->
# V3-Paper-Release – maßgeblicher aktueller Fachowner-Vertrag (09.11.2026)

**Autorität:** Dieses Issue #99 trifft ausschließlich die bereits vertraglich getrennten fachlichen Release-Entscheidungen. Es ist **keine** automatische Ausgabe eines neuen Stage4-, STOP-, CAS-, Reader-, Lease- oder Aktivierungs-Scope. Issue #353 bestimmt projektweit den Arbeitseinstieg. **Der einzige aktuelle, fortgeschriebene AP-Status steht [hier](https://github.com/hoffmannherdecke/kraken-eur-scanner/issues/353#issuecomment-6742581400).** Alte untenstehende PR695-/PR664-/PR661-„AKTUELL“-Abschnitte sind archivierte Originalzustände und niemals die heutige Arbeitswahl.

## Verbindliche Quellen- und Ausführungsreihenfolge
1. Vor jeder V3-Aktion **frischen** GitHub-main-HEAD, aktuellen kanonischen AP-Status, diesen Owner und für physische Schritte aktuelle Originalhost-/Cloud-/Notebook-Bindungen lesen. GitHub-Kommentar, Build/CI und Textdatum sind allein kein Live-Betriebs-ACK. Bei Widerspruch oder fehlendem Zugriff fail-closed HOLD im einzigen betroffenen AP, **kein** Fallback auf alte FIRST/NEXT-Texte.
2. **AP00 DONE:** PR #699 erlaubt unabhängig verifizierte isolierte E2E-Ersatzfälle für historisch nicht existierende V2R4-/Nach-Cutover-BUY-/Exit-/Aftercare-Teilfälle; echter neuer Single-Writer-/Runtime-Beleg bleibt Pflicht. PR #700/#701 sind auf main `46c5abbd6af16266c1229943db973dc9d6b2fb4f`; genehmigtes korrigiertes Paket `PR701-Nachfolge-Fix-NICHT-STARTEN.zip` SHA256 `04b62cd1f6df4d4e1e4e4fa7b57c060d7ba970542abc8f280cca791d60bf2d2a` ist **nur für Vorfensterbereitung** freigegeben in [Kommentar #6740338226](https://github.com/hoffmannherdecke/kraken-eur-scanner/issues/99#issuecomment-6740338226). Host-Staging/Nachfolgerbindung statisch bestätigt, aber kein Go-Live.
3. **AP01 NEXT, keine neue Entwicklungsphase:** Bestehende PR699/700-Originale in bereits bekanntem Work-/Host-Arbeitsbaum exakt an den freigegebenen PR701-Builder binden; zulässige reale Cloud-read-only-Rolle/Host-Originaldaten **vor** kurzlebiger Serienausgabe zuordnen. Bei unzugänglicher Work-Umgebung nur enger Access-HOLD, keine erdachten Dateien oder neuen Cloud-Berechtigungen. Danach AP02 endgültige Geräte-/Eingabeblöcke und Zeitbudget vorab, AP03 einmalige frische ≤90s-Originale und Fenster-ZIP, AP04 gesonderte stage4-seriengebundene neue Hash-/Plan-/Dryrun-Ownerentscheidung.
4. Nach tatsächlichem Stage4-ACK: **AP05A** Prepare/STOP und unabhängiger Reader; **AP05B** Stage5/einmaliger CAS/Executor-Close; **AP05C** Post-CAS-Reader/Runtime-Lease; **AP06A** gesonderte native V3-Aktivierung; **AP06B** reale wiederholte Host-/Cloud-Scanner-/Paper-/Heartbeat-/Single-Writer-Quittungen bis `V3_PAPER_OPERATIONAL`. Jedes AP nur mit echtem Nachweis freischalten.
5. Historische terminale Epoche `V3CAS-AUDIT-f4bc92a692174525bdb084b4e72db82f`: `ABORT_RECORDED_NOT_RELEASED`, null Intents/CAS, nicht neu öffnen; alter Fenster-ZIP und alte Serienentscheidungen nie wiederverwenden. Fehlende neue physische Originale und zeitgebundene Signaturen werden im jeweiligen aktuellen Gate erzeugt, nicht behauptet.
6. Kein Blind-Retry bei UNKNOWN, keine Secrets im Chat oder in ZIPs, keine Echtgeldausführung, keine kostenpflichtigen APIs, Notebook nur unabhängig punktuell; Mini-PC alleiniger produktiver Writer. Release-Code/Commit-/Zipänderungen benötigen die entsprechenden bestehenden getrennten technischen Prüfungen und Releasescopes.

Die jüngste Recovery hat bewiesen, dass lokale Prozesse überwacht und wiederhergestellt werden können und die atomare Paper-Serienrotation fail-closed bleibt. **Sie hat nicht bewiesen, dass die Architektur jeden Einzel-/Drittanbieterausfall autonom übersteht.** Das muss als eigener, sichtbarer Weiterentwicklungspunkt erhalten bleiben, ohne den stabilisierten Betrieb sofort wieder umzubauen.

- **Definierte Degradationsmodi:** Was darf autonom weiterlaufen; wann nur Beobachtung/Paper pausieren; niemals Real-Money-Fail-open. Eine ausgefallene optionale Datenquelle darf keine unbemerkte pauschale Kauf-/REJECT-Sperre erzeugen.
- **Wiederanlauf und Datenintegrität:** Begrenzte Backoff-/Retry-Strategie ohne Restart-Storm, idempotente Weiterverarbeitung, exakte Kurs-/Event-Zeiten und Lückenerkennung, getrennte Bezeichnung `UNAVAILABLE`/`UNKNOWN` vs. `NO_SIGNAL`; fehlende Echtzeitdaten nicht rückdatieren oder erfinden; selektives Backfill nur wenn sicher möglich und markiert.
- **Cloud/Local Failover-Eigenschaften:** Mini-PC bleibt SPOF, sofern kein separater redundanter Host/evidenzbasierter Wiederanlauf existiert. Kosten/Nutzen von minimalem Failover oder Recovery-Runbook bewerten, **keine vorschnelle Parallel-Infrastruktur** und keine doppelten Paper-Schreiber.
- **Messbare SLO/Gates:** maximale akzeptierte Statuslatenz, Fehlererkennung, Mean Time to Recovery, eindeutige Task-/Serienidentität, Dead-letter/Retry-Fälle, Zustellqualität, begrenzte Speicher-/API-Kosten.
- **Drittanbieter-Abhängigkeiten und Kontingente:** Ausfall/Rate limits/Quoten erkennen; GitHub- und andere Kostenkontingente; nur definierte, sichere Fallbacks.

### Vorgehen / Abschlusskriterien
1. Nach mindestens ~7 Tagen neuem Paper-Betrieb die vorhandenen Heartbeats, Restart-History, Ausfall-/Datenlücken und #89-Evidenz **nur lesen**; keine umfangreichen künstlichen Tests oder Voll-Audits.
2. Die Risiken als `BEREITS ABGEDECKT` / `TEILWEISE` / `OFFEN` klassifizieren. Nur **nachgewiesene** Lücken priorisieren: Schutz vor stillen Datenlücken, robustes begrenztes Recovery, dann Drittanbieter-Unabhängigkeit – in dieser Reihenfolge nach Nutzen/Risiko.
3. Höchstens einen kleinen, isolierten, reversiblen Verbesserungsschritt je nachgewiesenem Blocker als separaten PR/Shadow-Test vorbereiten, mit passender gezielter Regression und Rollback. Keine Strategieregel-, Threshold-/Sizing-, produktive Release- oder Echtgeldänderung ohne eigenes Gate.

**Verbindlich:** Keine Änderung an der aktiven Paper-Serie, H3-Historie, Produktions-Tasks, Supabase-Secrets oder Drittanbieter-Konfiguration allein durch dieses Issue. Keine zusätzliche teure Work-Schleife; nur bestehende Evidence nutzen. raw.title: SC-DISCOVERY-TOURNAMENT-001: prospective, synthesis-aware superconductivity discovery benchmark
raw.body:
## Objective

Create a **prospective, leakage-resistant, decision-centric benchmark** for superconductivity discovery. The benchmark evaluates whether a method finds more scientifically credible and synthesizable candidates at a fixed compute / validation budget—not merely whether it achieves a low retrospective Tc MAE.

Parent: [SC-AMB-PRESSURE-001 #12617](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/12617).

## Why this is a new work package

The current frontier contains several incompatible prediction tasks that must not be collapsed into one leaderboard:

- **BEE-NET** predicts conventional electron–phonon / Eliashberg quantities against DFT/Allen–Dynes labels; it reports 0.87 K MAE on that computational target. This is not measured experimental Tc.
- **Genome-inspired AI (29 October 2026)** reports a 53,196-material DataG Non-Sc dataset and screens candidates across ICSD, COD and Materials Project. Its reported Pu-based and hydride candidates are predictions, not independently confirmed superconductors. The early-access paper version and dataset/checkpoint reproducibility need independent audit.
- **HTSC-2025** is a separate 155-material benchmark of predicted ambient-pressure high-Tc candidates; its evaluation target and system-specific structural splits must remain separate from measured experimental Tc.
- **Matbench Discovery** provides a useful methodological precedent: measure discovery utility along a ranked validation campaign (precision/recall vs K and discovery acceleration), not only global regression error. Its reported crystal-stability score is not a superconductivity result and must not be compared numerically with one.

A common benchmark can compare decision quality while preserving mechanism-specific model tracks and target provenance.

## Paradigm shift

Replace the simple 'predict Tc and sort descending' approach with a gated decision pipeline:

candidate universe -> identity/dedup -> mechanism track -> electronic/structural plausibility -> synthesis/phase-retention gate -> pressure/temperature operating envelope -> calibrated uncertainty/OOD abstention -> budgeted candidate selection -> independent verification -> engineering translation.

No single weighted score may compensate for a failed hard constraint (for example, a material that only exists at extreme pressure cannot rank as an ambient-pressure operating candidate).

## Tracks — do not mix target labels

1. **Conventional electron–phonon:** alpha2F(omega), lambda, omega_log, pressure-resolved phonons, dynamical stability and Allen–Dynes/Eliashberg estimates. BEE-NET is a primary baseline here.
2. **Correlated / unconventional:** cuprates, nickelates, iron-based and engineered-interface systems. Keep theory and observable models explicit; do not force an electron–phonon Tc oracle where the mechanism is not established.
3. **Hydrides / pressure-dependent:** store synthesis pressure, operating pressure, decompression path, metastability and retention separately.
4. **Empirical composition / structure classification:** evaluate DataG Non-Sc, SuperCon-derived data and related approaches with formula/family/prototype/source grouping and strict label provenance.
5. **Experimental reference cases:** same-specimen transport, magnetic and (where available) thermodynamic measurements; distinguish onset, zero resistance, diamagnetic/Meissner and bulk transitions.

## Benchmark requirements

### A. Dataset integrity and leakage resistance

- Freeze exact source revisions, retrieval dates, licenses, schemas and hashes.
- Resolve formula aliases, reduced formula, structure prototype, polymorph, dopant series, sample/batch and repeated measurement identities.
- Group splits by reduced chemical system, parent family, structure prototype and source/lab where appropriate; add leave-family-out, chemistry-held-out, temporal/source-held-out and pressure-held-out tests.
- Keep all preprocessing, feature selection, calibration and hyperparameter selection inside training folds.
- Report the independent unit count (materials, prototypes, batches and specimens), not only row count.
- Include both superconducting and non-superconducting controls; preserve ambiguous, non-converged and failed cases.
- Freeze prospective candidate lists before running expensive first-principles calculations or querying external evidence.

### B. Decision metrics at fixed budgets

For K = 10, 25, 50, 100 and 500 candidates, report:
- precision@K / validated-candidate yield@K;
- discovery acceleration factor versus random selection and simple chemistry heuristics;
- cumulative recall where a defensible denominator exists;
- novelty by chemical family/prototype, not merely novel formula strings;
- calibration, Brier score / log loss, selective risk and coverage;
- OOD detection and useful abstention rate;
- synthesis/phase-retention success, false-positive burden and cost per independently validated result;
- Pareto frontier across Tc, operating pressure, synthesisability, uncertainty, critical-element burden, safety and engineering potential.

Report confidence intervals and paired comparisons on identical frozen candidate pools. A model that abstains on unfamiliar candidates should be rewarded for calibrated honesty, not punished as though it made a confident wrong prediction.

### C. Synthesis and physical truth gates

For every candidate preserve separate values for:
- predicted Tc vs calculated Tc vs observed Tc;
- onset vs zero-resistance vs diamagnetic/Meissner vs thermodynamic/bulk transition;
- synthesis pressure vs operating pressure vs decompression-retention pressure;
- 0 K hull distance vs finite-temperature phase stability vs kinetic/metastable lifetime;
- calculated dynamical stability vs experimentally synthesized phase;
- structure/purity/stoichiometry evidence and the exact sample identity joining measurements.

The same specimen/batch identity must join structural, transport and magnetic observations. Never combine different samples' strongest measurements to fabricate one bulk confirmation.

### D. Safety and resource-aware candidate selection

- Default-exclude radioactive actinide candidates, highly toxic compositions, and candidates requiring exceptional containment from ordinary experimental shortlists. They may remain in a clearly marked computational-only research lane pending qualified institutional review.
- Account for critical-element scarcity, precursor availability, process temperature/pressure, equipment availability, energy input and plausible scale.
- Do not publish a synthesis route or experimental operating procedure in this benchmark issue; a candidate ranking is not synthesis authorization.

## New 2026 evidence cases to add

- **Ambient-pressure nickelate film:** (La,Pr)3Ni2O7; reported Tc onset ~63 K, zero-resistance ~37 K and diamagnetic transition beginning ~23 K. These are three different observables from the same research context, not one 63 K bulk transition. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwag151
- **Pressure-induced bulk nickelate:** La2SmNi2O7−delta; crystals synthesized at ambient pressure, but superconductivity reported at ~21.6 GPa (onset 92 K, zero 73 K) and Meissner response at 60 K / 20.6 GPa. Ambient-pressure synthesis is not ambient-pressure operation. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09954-4
- **Hydrogen-unit hydrides:** CaAuH6 is predicted at 44 K at ambient pressure and 70 K at 30 GPa in a 2026 computational study. This remains a theoretical prediction, not a measured material. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtphys.2026.102142
- **Genome-inspired AI candidates:** the 29 October 2026 early-access paper predicts >50 K in 22 Pu-based candidates (including Pu2Co17 ~89 K) and up to 100 K in hydrides. No experimental confirmation is claimed in the abstract; Pu candidates remain computational-only by default. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-76977-w

## Proposed performance targets (research targets, not results)

1. Reproduce each baseline on its own exact published dataset, split, label and metric before modifying it.
2. Beat the strongest baseline on **family-held-out and prospective top-K yield**, with paired confidence intervals, rather than relying on random-split MAE alone.
3. Stretch target: at K <= 50, achieve >= 1.5x the validated-candidate enrichment of the strongest admitted baseline on a frozen prospective pool, without worsening OOD calibration or safety/operating-pressure constraints. If the validation cohort is too small for meaningful confidence intervals, report the result as inconclusive rather than relaxing the gate.
4. At fixed compute budget, reduce expensive DFT/experimental follow-up per independently verified candidate by >= 2x versus the best simple heuristic. This must be demonstrated on a prospective cohort.
5. No candidate is promoted to an engineering material without conductor/device metrics and an application-matched comparison against NbTi, Nb3Sn, MgB2 and REBCO.

## Immediate offline increments

- Create a versioned machine-readable source/candidate register with evidence classes, separate Tc observables and pressure semantics.
- Pin the current BEE-NET Git commit and audit artifact/split access through #12619.
- Request/resolve the DataG Non-Sc dataset, model weights, train/test manifest, feature-generation code and exact definition of a negative label before admitting its metrics.
- Define grouped and prospective splits with explicit candidate-budget curves.
- Create a small, hand-auditable control set and adversarial leakage tests before training a new model.
- Keep Symthaea MAT-RD / MAT-MLIP as material physics owners; Symtropy owns replayable simulation and physical-service translation; #11736 owns REBCO conductor-to-coil engineering.

## Claim ceiling

This issue creates a benchmark design and literature register only. It does not reproduce BEE-NET or the new genome-inspired model, perform DFT/Eliashberg calculations, synthesize a material, or validate any predicted candidate experimentally. A passing offline benchmark is not a superconductivity discovery.

raw.title: Mission 12 — Mining & Power — Season II

labels.name: source:h2
labels.description: Demand exposed by Telegraph Hackathon Season II

raw.body:
**Start with the customer and work backwards.** This mission is about delivering something useful, not accumulating disconnected Intents or registrations. A contributor can build the whole solution—application, intelligence Provider and relevant evaluation work—or concentrate on one part and work with others. All three hackathon tracks are open, with separate qualifying entries under the [official rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules).

## The opportunity

**Who it serves:** Bitcoin miners, grid operators and AI compute/data-center operators.

**Problem:** Hashing versus compute allocation and energy curtailment rely on fragmented priced data and are hard to audit.

**A useful result:** An hourly allocation, curtailment or telemetry-to-evidence workflow where each input and decision is time-stamped, priced and reproducible.

Pick a specific customer and workflow. Establish the alternative they use today, a realistic willingness-to-pay or budget constraint, a measurable result, acceptable error and response time. These are example opportunities, not exclusive products or confirmed customers. See [Mining & Power](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions/mining-and-power) and the [full mission catalogue](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/missions).

| Route | Actual outcome to build | Shared capability families to investigate and use |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Hourly mining/compute allocation** | Buy hashprice and grid price evidence, compare with a disclosed compute alternative, and generate an auditable site-by-site recommendation. | `MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY`, `GRID_POWER_PRICE`, `WEB_SEARCH` |
| **2. Collateral decision with evidence** | Buy reserve/registry/risk checks before a simulated collateral pledge, preserving a decision trace. | `ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION`, `CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP`, `FINANCIAL_DATA` |
| **3. Operator telemetry as paid supply** | Publish anonymized, authorized power/temperature/utilization telemetry as a Miner and demonstrate paid external query. | `SENSOR_TELEMETRY_VERIFY`, `DATACENTER_TELEMETRY_VERIFY` |

**First milestone:** one realistic input → a paid Telegraph intelligence request → a checked result with its source/uncertainty → a useful action or answer → receipt and total cost. Include one failure case before expanding the workflow. You do **not** need to implement all three example products.

**Tests worth demonstrating:** Simulate a negative-price hour, stale power price, telemetry outage and a budget-cap breach; do not state real energy was dispatched unless it was.

**Measures that matter:** Estimated margin per MWh, cost per allocation decision, SLA verification reliability, forecast timestamp precision.

## Intelligence needed

**Published starting families:** `GRID_POWER_PRICE`, `MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY`, `DATACENTER_TELEMETRY_VERIFY`, `SLA_COMPLIANCE`, `SENSOR_TELEMETRY_VERIFY`, `WEATHER_FORECAST_VERIFY`, `VALIDATOR_PERFORMANCE_VERIFY`, `ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION`, `TRANSACTION_RISK`, `MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR`.

These are shared network capabilities, **not separate bounties** created for this mission. The same capability may support several missions, with one canonical Intent, one Provider market and one evaluation pool. The list is a starting map, not a mandatory bill of materials or proof of live coverage.

Before implementing anything, inspect the [live canonical Intent list](https://devnode.telegraphprotocol.com/engine/v1/intents), [request and response schemas](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema), [ranked Providers](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/explore) and [published Intent catalogue](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/INTENTS.md). Use the **exact** live `intent_name` and `request.params`; family names and guessed `_GENERAL` suffixes are not reliable request identifiers. Some unknown names return HTTP 200 with a null schema, which is not a working Intent. The [mission mapping](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/blob/main/docs/MISSIONS.md) is helpful for discovery, but the node determines which capabilities are callable and what evaluation path applies.

A finished report, dashboard, refund, memo or decision is usually **application composition**, not a new protocol Intent. Use existing reusable capabilities first. Only propose a new Intent for genuinely reusable intelligence missing from the catalogue.

## Ways to contribute

### Apps & Agents — deliver the product

Build a runnable application that **autonomously purchases or sells intelligence through Telegraph** and uses the response to complete a meaningful task. Start with the smallest useful customer workflow; confirm the supporting Intents and live Provider quality before committing to an architecture.

Choose the right [delivery path](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/inference-paths): [Engine Ask](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/engine-ask) for fresh on-demand work; [x402](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/x402-inference) or [escrow](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/escrow-inference) for supported settlement; [WebSocket Signals](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/websocket-signals) when reusable streamed intelligence is appropriate; [MCP](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/mcp-server) for integrations. A Signal subscription is not a substitute for a fresh, user-specific check. A 402 payment challenge is not evidence of a completed purchase.

Make uncertainty visible. Handle partial or conflicting answers, stale data, missing Providers, spending limits and failures. Prove the total **cost per useful completed outcome** rather than multiplying paid requests unnecessarily. Reuse valid fresh intelligence when permitted; avoid paying repeatedly for the same shared fact. Irreversible transactions and sensitive actions require the user's authorization. Simulated or testnet behavior must be labelled as such.

**Completion evidence:** runnable app and instructions, a new realistic input producing a useful result, authentic Telegraph request/payment evidence, costs and latency, and a reproducible failure case. A static interface or a Miner registration alone does not qualify as the app.

### Miners / Providers — supply the intelligence

Identify a missing or weak capability for this customer workflow. Test existing Providers to understand the quality bar. Independent competing implementations for the same canonical Intent are welcome; show how yours performs in accuracy, coverage, freshness, price, reliability or latency. Implement a callable service for a supported canonical Intent, following its actual request/response schema and [Miner YAML guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/yaml-config).

Check the [validation guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/validation-api) and current [registration steps](https://anjoman.ai/docs/miners/miner-registration). **Known documentation limitation (Nov 15):** the guide says its `POST /dashboard/validate` endpoint currently returns 404; use the available web checks, documented local checks and supported registration dry-run instead of treating that POST as working. Use the [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet) for eligible testnet needs. Confirm the registration is active and the service answers the actual Intent; capture its registration ID, test cases, measured results and paid request evidence. Distinguish direct diagnostic requests from selection by ranked routing.

Share working endpoints and registration IDs here so other applications and missions can reuse the Provider.

### Evaluators — measure whether the intelligence is good

Use the selected Intent's **actual node class, family and scoring path**, not the name or an old bounty description, to determine what's needed:

- **Deterministic:** reliable public truth-source material and the supported comparator path. A new judgment adapter is not inherently required.
- **Hybrid:** the checkable truth source/comparator and judgment contribution that the live scoring path actually uses.
- **Judgment:** sourced, balanced better/worse examples and a compatible evaluation adapter **where needed**. Do not assume every Intent needs a new adapter plus material.

Contribute through [Anjoman Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval), following [material formats and provenance](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/contribute-evaluation-data) and the [scoring-module guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/build-a-scoring-module) when applicable. Use primary evidence, timestamps, block/chain or jurisdiction identifiers, correct units and tolerances. Include correct, incorrect, incomplete and ambiguous cases; avoid datasets solvable merely by answer length, keywords or copied prompt wording. Test on unseen sources and failure types. Confirm **eligible / rejected** material state and actual module status separately; passing a local test or uploading rows does not imply canonical promotion.

A single project may contribute a working app, a Provider and genuinely useful evaluation work. Each track still requires its own qualifying evidence. No extra or duplicative component is needed simply to claim participation across all three.

## Share work here as it happens

**Read the latest comments and existing [Bounties Issues](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties/issues) to understand current activity, available capabilities and opportunities to collaborate.** Multiple contributors are welcome to independently build applications, Providers and Evaluators for the same mission or Intent, including competing implementations. Existing work does not reserve a mission, product or Intent. Share progress and findings so others can collaborate, reuse useful contributions or compete independently.

If using the existing Bounties workflow, post `/claim` and then a short comment identifying your scope. Claims are **non-exclusive**. Keep the thread current with `/progress <update>` at least every **72 hours** while claimed, and link relevant work from other mission threads. Useful updates include:

```text
Scope: [product or capability + customer problem]
Track(s): [Apps & Agents / Miners / Providers / Evaluators]
Working on: [concrete deliverable, canonical Intents if known]
Reusing (optional): [existing work, Providers, evaluations + links]
Approach: [what you are building and how you plan to deliver it]
Current state: [building / tested / blocked / submitted]
Proof or next milestone: [repo/demo/endpoint, reproducible result]
```

When ready, post `/submit <links and evidence>` for your individual contribution, **and** use the official Anjoman submission path. GitHub comments coordinate work; they are not the final hackathon entry or evaluation upload. One team's submission does not close the mission to other participants. Existing accepted contributions and claims remain valid; reviewers assess individual entries separately. Don't post credentials, private customer data, protected evaluation samples or sensitive exploit details.

## Prove it, share it, submit it

A strong entry can be tested by someone outside the team: provide a live demo or callable endpoint, public-safe repository, run instructions, real request IDs/receipts, one failure test, honest cost figures and limitations. For apps, explain what was purchased and **what useful action happened afterward**. Consider listing working apps in [Anjoman Apps](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/apps) for others to discover.

The [Season II judging rules](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon/season-2/rules) apply across all three tracks (100 points each; **70/100** overall and each track's stated technical minimum). Apps are scored on technical quality/mainnet readiness (35 points, minimum 24), commercial viability (25), independent adoption (10), integration and usage (5), reproducibility (5), and organic growth/developer activation (20). Providers and Evaluators have their **own** track rubrics on the same rules page.

The 20 growth points cover **useful education (5), ease of adoption (5), organic distribution (5), and independent community activation (5)**. Share a working explanation or video, a genuinely useful walkthrough, and **at least three meaningful original progress updates on separate dates**. Invite independent developers to try, reproduce or integrate your work; show their real feedback and results. Publish where relevant (GitHub, Discord, X, technical communities) and follow the published tagging/link guidance. Bought engagement, fake traffic, manipulated stars, self-dealing and fabricated demand do not count. **Star the [Bounties repository](https://github.com/telegraphprotocol/bounties)** as required in Section 5; this is an entry requirement, not proof of growth.

**Prizes and possible earnings:** $7,000 for the Season II main competition ($3,000 Apps, $2,000 Providers, $2,000 Evaluators), plus $3,000 reserved for separate December challenges—not an extra automatic Season II pool. Awards depend on eligibility and verification. Beyond prizes, eligible Providers may earn from paid usage, Evaluator contributions may earn applicable protocol rewards, and products may generate revenue if customers adopt them. **Nothing is guaranteed** by a claim, registration or testnet call. This is a coordination Issue, not a separately funded GitHub bounty.

**Deadline:** **December 1, 2026, 23:59 UTC** for the main competition; **November 20** is the progress showcase. Finish the [official H2 submission](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/hackathon) using its live form when available, selecting the tracks and attaching distinct evidence for each. As of November 15, the site says the final form opens later; don't mistake a GitHub `/submit` comment for the final submission. The official rules control eligibility, awards, dates and any subsequent announcements.

## Before reporting a blocker

| Problem | Check first |
|---|---|
| Intent request fails or returns an empty schema | Select an exact live canonical Intent; inspect `request.params`, response fields and active Provider coverage in the [schema guide](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intent-schema). A 200 response with `request: null` is not a valid Intent. |
| No result after x402 or escrow | Follow the documented full payment flow; a 402 offer alone is not a settled purchase. Check available receipt and account evidence. |
| A Miner looks highly ranked but answers the wrong question | Reproduce the input, preserve the raw/shaped result and actual receipt, compare with a direct diagnostic call, and report the specific ranking gap. |
| Registration, validation or bond trouble | Check the registration and validation docs, live node state, chain configuration and [faucet](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/faucet); the documented `POST /dashboard/validate` route is currently flagged as broken. |
| Evaluation material or module rejected | Check eligible/rejected reasons, provenance, required shape, supported family kind and public scoring requirements; don't infer adapter requirements from an Intent's label. |
| A similar app or capability already exists | Independent competing implementations are welcome. Review existing work for useful references, reuse or collaborate where appropriate, or proceed independently. No exclusive claims. |

For a genuine unresolved protocol defect, post a concise reproducible report here (exact Intent, public request, expected/actual behavior and safe evidence), then use [Discord](https://discord.gg/telegraphprotocol) for escalation if necessary.

## Done when

- [ ] A real customer need and runnable app/agent that solves it are demonstrated.
- [ ] A supported paid Telegraph request/sale leads to a useful action, with authentic receipt/accounting evidence.
- [ ] Relevant shared Intents have usable Provider supply and evaluation coverage, or precisely documented remaining gaps.
- [ ] A reviewer can reproduce a realistic success and failure case, including total cost and latency.
- [ ] Contributors' progress and relevant final entries are linked in comments; evidence distinguishes testnet, production and genuine external adoption.

This checklist measures **mission coverage**, not one person's prize eligibility. A successful app does not imply every possible workflow or every mapped Intent is complete. Keep this Issue available for distinct contributors; do not close it merely because one scope finished.

## Reward

**No standalone GitHub payout.** Season II prizes and ongoing protocol earnings are separate and governed by their published eligibility and payment terms.

raw.body:
## What's wrong

An Answer's sentence keeps its ✓ when it states a percent and the words it cites give percentage points, or the other way round. Six percentage points is not six percent (from 10% to 16% is a rise of 60%), so this is a wrong ✓ on the User's own Documents.

Check against Documents catches the same sentences: it runs the unit guard from #1452 and says "The Document gives 6 percentage points, not 6%." The Answer's own sentence check does not. Its calculation gate (`src/core/answers/checks/calculationGate.ts`) asks `unitNotStated` about each figure and, when the unit is not stated, skips that figure; nothing after the gate in `answerCheck.ts` runs the unit gate (`unitGate.ts` is used by `claimCheck.ts` only). So a model's "supported" stands.

Found while reviewing #2992. Run through the core on `main`, with a model reply of "supported", each sentence citing a Document's own words:

| Sentence | The Document says | In the Answer | Check against Documents |
|---|---|---|---|
| It rose 6%. | It rose 6 percentage points. | ✓ | Unsupported: "The Document gives 6 percentage points, not 6%." |
| It rose 20%. | The index rose 20 points. | ✓ | Unsupported: "The Document gives 20 points, not 20%." |
| It rose 6 percentage points. | It rose 6%. | ✓ | Unsupported: "The Document gives 6%, not 6 percentage points." |

As controls, "It rose 7%." and "It rose 7 percentage points." citing "It rose 6 percentage points." are not judged.

`unitNotStated` also covers a currency on a plain number, another scale of the same written number and a named dollar on a bare "$" (#1452, #2226). The gate skips those the same way, so they may keep a ✓ in an Answer too; the first part measures that.

## Parts

- [x] **Measured first.** Every case in the tests of #1452 and #2226, and the three rows above, run through the Answer's sentence check with a "supported" reply: the pull request lists each with its verdict on `main`. On a real model, how many of those pairs the model itself calls supported today, with the model named.
- [x] **A percent is not backed by percentage points, nor points by a percent.** The three rows above no longer end as ✓ in an Answer. The pull request says what they end as (Unsupported with the reason Check against Documents gives, or Not checked) and why; the same in Chinese (百分点 against %).
- [ ] **The other unit cases the measurement finds.** Each case that ends ✓ in an Answer and Unsupported in Check against Documents ends the same in both.
- [x] **An organisation's name after 编制单位： that begins with a scale and a unit word.** «编制单位：千台精工有限公司» over «单位：元» still reads the name's 千台 as the Document's scale and unit, on `main` and with the organisation-after-colon guard alike. **Closed as a known cost (2026-11-16):** in a count of 40 published tables, none of the three organisation lines met has such a name. Its neighbours (万元集团, 千瓦科技有限公司) are pinned by the test "known costs of an organisation named after a colon", and this name joins them in #3238.
- [x] **One guard.** The Answer's check and Check against Documents use the same unit gate, not a second copy.
- [x] **Twins keep their ✓.** "It rose 6%." citing "It rose 6%."; "It rose 6 percentage points." citing "It rose 6 percentage points."; "230 bps" citing "2.3 percentage points"; a currency the Document states.
- [x] **It only takes a ✓ away.** Over the sentences in the repo's tests and evaluation sets, the pull request lists every Answer verdict that changes. None goes from not ✓ to ✓.

## For all parts

English and Chinese. Documents and a Meeting's Transcript alike: since #2992 a number said before "percentage points" stays in words in a Transcript because of this; once this holds, say in the pull request whether it can be written as "6 percentage points" again. This changes a check's verdict, so someone other than the builder reads it before it merges.

raw.title: perf(settings): speed up native Settings window open (entry code-split, warm WebView reuse, single-IPC bootstrap, and batched registrations)
raw.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched [existing issues](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and this hasn't been requested yet.

### Problem

Opening **Settings…** (`⌘,` / `OpenIDEA › Settings…` from the application menu) has noticeable latency before the Settings window appears and finishes rendering its page tree and form. Tracing the end-to-end open path at [`76377b6ee`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/tree/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af) shows four compounding bottlenecks:

1. **Every open cold-boots a brand-new `WKWebView` (destroyed on close) after a Rust → parent JS → Rust menu bounce:**
   - Choosing **Settings…** from the native menu runs [`dispatch_menu_action` (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:378–403`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src-tauri/src/lib.rs#L378-L403), which emits `openidea://menu` to the parent window's WebView JS thread, waits for JS to run [`showSettings` (`src/features/settings/index.ts:104–110`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/settings/index.ts#L104-L110), and calls `window_open_settings` right back into Rust. If the parent window's main thread is busy, window creation stalls before starting.
   - Closing Settings via OK / Cancel / `Esc` runs [`getCurrentWebviewWindow().close()` (`src/features/settings/index.ts:227`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/settings/index.ts#L227), destroying `settings-<parent>` ([`src-tauri/src/windows.rs:1502–1590`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src-tauri/src/windows.rs#L1502-L1590)). Every subsequent `⌘,` pays full OS WebView process/VM creation, HTML/CSS fetch, JS parse/compile, and state hydration from scratch.

2. **Monolithic entry bundle loads & evaluates all 46 IDE features (~5.80 MB / 127 preloaded files) inside the Settings WebView:**
   - `settings-<parent>` loads `index.html` → [`src/main.tsx`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/main.tsx#L4-L16). Even though [`src/main.tsx:57`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/main.tsx#L57) branches on `aux?.kind === "settings"` to skip *calling* `activateWorkbench()` / `activateFeatures()`, `main.tsx` statically imports `./workbench/Workbench` and [`./features/index.ts:7–56`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/index.ts#L7-L56)—which statically imports all 46 workbench features (`editor` / CodeMirror 6, `editorLsp`, `vcs` / GitLog / blame, `terminal`, `debugger`, `profiler` / `HeapCapture`, `notebook`, `database`, `agents`, etc.).
   - In a production `vite build`, `dist/index.html` includes **127 entry + `<link rel="modulepreload">` + CSS assets totaling ~5.80 MB uncompressed** (`index-*.js` = 2.34 MB, `ui-*.js` = 1.36 MB, `index-*.css` = 255 KB) that WebKit must fetch, link, parse, and evaluate before `SettingsWindow` renders.

3. **Sequential 4-IPC startup waterfall (including SSH round-trips in Remote Development) + eager import of all built-in page UIs blocks `pagesLoading: false`:**
   - While `pagesLoading: true` replaces the layout with `<Spinner /> Loading…` ([`SettingsDialog.tsx:314–320`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/settings/dialog/SettingsDialog.tsx#L314-L320)), [`activateSettingsWindow` (`src/features/settings/index.ts:235–257`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/settings/index.ts#L235-L257) awaits in sequence:
     1. `await takeLaunch()` (`window_take_launch` — awaited *before* starting `loadBuiltinPages()` or project/settings calls)
     2. `await restoreRemote()` (`remote_current`)
     3. `await commands.projectCurrent()` — in a remote window ([`src/platform/remote.ts:112–117`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/platform/remote.ts#L112-L117), [`crates/ide-host/src/rpc.rs:158`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/crates/ide-host/src/rpc.rs#L158)), `project_current` routes over SSH to `openidea-server` and *then* sequentially awaits local `settings_get_global`
     4. `rebaseSettings()` → `loadGlobalBase()` (calls `settings_get_global` a second time)
   - Meanwhile, [`src/features/settings/pages/registry.tsx:6–17`](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/settings/pages/registry.tsx#L6-L17) statically imports **every** built-in settings page UI (~267 KB `registry-*.js`: Keymap, File Types, Inspections, Code Style, Color Scheme, Deployment, SSH, Languages) upfront rather than lazy-loading non-active page bodies.

4. **Unbatched *O*(*N*²) Zustand `Map` clones & startup IPC contention on first paint:**
   - [`installActionProxies` (`src/features/settings/window/bridge.ts:104–108`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/settings/window/bridge.ts#L104-L108) loops over all ~500+ parent actions calling singular `registerAction(proxy)` instead of batched [`registerActions(...)` (`src/platform/actions.ts:141–153`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/platform/actions.ts#L141-L153)—cloning `new Map(s.actions)` and running `localize(action)` 500+ times synchronously.
   - [`registerSettingsPage` (`src/workbench/contributions.ts:1194–1195`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/workbench/contributions.ts#L1194-L1195) similarly clones `new Map(s.pages)` ~80+ times individually (built-in pages + async `codeStyleLanguagePages()`), while [`pluginsPages` (`src/features/plugins/index.ts:75`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/features/plugins/index.ts#L75) triggers `refreshPlugins()` and the default Appearance page's [`FontPicker` (`src/platform/systemFonts.ts:42–69`)](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/openidea/blob/76377b6eecb3931273024bbab8751832adda51af/src/platform/systemFonts.ts#L42-L69) triggers `system_font_families` immediately on mount.

### Proposed solution

1. **Split auxiliary window boot out of the Workbench module graph (`src/main.tsx`):**
   - Check `auxiliaryWindow()` in `src/main.tsx` *before* importing Workbench or `src/features/index.ts`, dynamically importing a lightweight `./settingsMain` (or dedicated Vite multi-page HTML entry) that pulls in only `platform`, `ui` form/tree primitives, and settings-page contributions instead of all 46 workbench/editor features.

2. **Keep `settings-<parent>` warm (hide on close) + open directly from Rust on native menu click:**
   - In `dispatch_menu_action` (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs`), when `id` is `"file.settings"` or `"file.newProjectsSettings"` and `global_settings.effective().appearance.settings_in_separate_window` is true, call `windows::open_settings_window` directly in Rust without bouncing through the parent WebView's JS main thread.
   - On Cancel / OK / `Esc` / native `CloseRequested` for `settings-<parent>`, discard staged edits and hide the window (`window.hide()`, returning focus to `parent`) rather than destroying the `WKWebView`, destroying it only when its parent project window closes or when the setting is toggled off. Repeat `⌘,` opens become sub-frame (`< 16 ms`).

3. **Single-IPC local bootstrap snapshot + lazy built-in page bodies:**
   - Add a single local command (e.g., `window_take_settings_init`) returning `{ launch, remoteSession, project, effectiveSettings, globalSettings }` from local desktop state in one round-trip—eliminating the 4-call waterfall and avoiding any blocking SSH `project_current` round-trip before first paint (refreshing remote project state asynchronously if needed).
   - Keep lightweight page metadata and search/option labels synchronous in `registry.tsx` (so sidebar tree rendering and settings search remain instant), while wrapping heavy page components (`KeymapPage`, `Inspections`, `CodeStyle`, `ColorScheme`, `FileTypes`, `Languages`, `SSH`, `Deployment`) in `lazyComponent`.

4. **Batch store registrations & defer font enumeration:**
   - Replace the per-item `registerAction(proxy)` loop in `src/features/settings/window/bridge.ts:104–108` with a single `registerActions(proxies)` call, and add batched `registerSettingsPages(pages)` in `src/workbench/contributions.ts`.
   - Defer `loadSystemFonts()` in `FontPicker.tsx` until idle (`requestIdleCallback` / `setTimeout`) or combobox open/focus (or pre-warm `ide_fonts::families(false)` once on a background thread after IDE launch).

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `settings-<parent>` boots through a code-split entry that does not import `Workbench`, CodeMirror editor bundles, or non-settings feature modules.
- [ ] Choosing **Settings…** from the native application menu when separate-window mode is active opens/focuses `settings-<parent>` directly in Rust without a parent-WebView round-trip, and closing Settings hides/reuses the warm window (cleaned up when its parent window closes).
- [ ] Cold Settings window startup initializes launch target, remote routing, and effective + global settings in one local IPC round-trip without blocking `pagesLoading: false` on remote SSH `project_current` calls or non-active settings page chunks.
- [ ] `installActionProxies` and `registerBuiltinPages` batch Zustand `Map` updates (`registerActions` / `registerSettingsPages`) instead of performing *O*(*N*²) per-entry `Map` clones.
- [ ] Add a `perf/` scenario (and budget in `perf/budgets.json`) measuring cold and warm Settings open latency (`settings.openColdMs`, `settings.openWarmMs`).

### Alternatives and workarounds

Turning off **Appearance & Behavior › Appearance › Open Settings in a separate window** avoids creating a second `WKWebView` (falling back to the in-page `LazySettingsDialog` overlay), though the first in-page open still pays for eager `loadBuiltinPages()` (`registry.tsx`) and unbatched `registerSettingsPage` updates.

### Additional context

- Complements #3790 (Settings / Project Structure organization) without changing any user-visible Settings layout or staging semantics.

raw.title: [AI COLLABORATION HUB] Shared task claims, ownership and handoffs
raw.body:
# FRIDAY Universe — Shared AI Collaboration Hub

This issue is the persistent, shared claim and handoff thread for every AI and human collaborator working in FRIDAY Universe.

## Authority and scope
- `docs/MASTER_PLAN.md` remains the source of project objectives, dependencies and acceptance criteria.
- `docs/collaboration/WORK_BOARD.yaml` is the operational mirror of task ownership and progress.
- `docs/collaboration/FILE_OWNERSHIP.yaml` records protected file/component claims.
- This issue is the externally visible coordination thread for claims, releases, blockers and handoffs. It is not a competing roadmap.

## Claim protocol
Before editing a task's files, post one top-level comment in this issue with:

```text
CLAIM TASK-ID
Collaborator: <registered collaborator ID>
Branch: <branch name>
PR: <number or none>
Files: <paths or components>
Started: <UTC ISO-8601>
Expected next update: <UTC ISO-8601>
```

A claim is active only after the branch and file list are recorded in the shared work board. Check for an existing active claim and overlapping file ownership first. Do not begin overlapping work while a claim is active unless the owner explicitly agrees in this thread.

For simultaneous claims, pause both edits and resolve ownership in this thread; do not assume that a local branch update constitutes a lock.

## Release / handoff protocol
Post:
- `RELEASE TASK-ID` when work is handed off or abandoned.
- `HANDOFF TASK-ID` with completed work, test evidence, branch/PR, blockers and the exact next action.
- `BLOCKED TASK-ID` with the dependency and who can unblock it.
- `REVIEW TASK-ID PR-NUMBER` with reproducible findings.

Claims must be renewed with a status update when the expected update time passes. A missing update does not authorize another collaborator to overwrite work; first contact the owner and preserve the branch.

## Safety
No force-pushes, blind resets, unapproved merges, production changes, secret disclosure or destructive operations. The project owner retains final approval for merges and deployments.

All collaborators — Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, ZAI, Vercel v0 and future contributors — are equal participants. Register actual tool/access capabilities; do not assume capabilities from a product name.

milestone.title: M29 ゴール指向方針の行動品質・費用改善の実証
milestone.description:
2026-10-18 最新状態：OpenCode 無料モデルによる6分類の初期判断 A/B 各1回を取得した。P3 の必要質問・P4 の権限確認・P6 の境界欠陥検出は両条件で維持したが、B にも不要な質問と根拠参照の誤りが残り、品質維持・全体効率の改善は判定保留。初期判断・計画案・供給ソースのレビューのみで、全工程の実装・回答反映・拒否後停止・修正後検証・外側操作者を含む費用は未測定。失敗・調整・評価費用を保存し、Issue と milestone は OPEN を維持する。

以下は初期設計と過去の追補であり、未実施という記述は各記録時点のもの。

ユーザーの最終成果へ、必要な品質・安全性を保って到達する。細かな設定質問や成果を改善しないロール間の往復を抑える共通・担当別方針、文書 acceptance、保存評価は PR #93 で実装済みだが、行動改善・全体費用の実測は未完了。ADR-0040 と #90 に比較設計・文献の確認範囲・停止条件を記録する。144実行を最小とする案、token・時間とも10%削減の固定基準は撤回。12実行は6分類・A/B各1回で評価手順を試す予備実験案で、実行承認や非劣性の証明ではない。同一実装で方針文だけを替え、文書 gate・権限・必須検証を共通にする。完了後の不要なロール再起動、必要確認の省略、失敗・再試行・Planner・操作者を含む全体費用を評価する。原稿・課題・独立判定・既存記録の不足をモデル実行なしに準備し、評価者と数値予算・期限・停止条件の確定後に予備実験を判断する。本実験はその結果と事前の判定基準で別に判断し、資料の整備だけで milestone を完了にしない。新評価基盤・追加モデル実行・tag・Release は今回開始しない。#90 と本 milestone は OPEN、次版番号・公開日は未確定。


2026-10-18 追補：利用者が Copilot model=auto の評価専用・読取り専用利用を許可したため、人手評価者の確保を予備実験の必須条件から外す。固定 rubric、発生機会別の分母、実装担当と別 session、条件名の盲検化、根拠付き構造化判定、自動テストと権限ログの照合を使う。LLMだけで重大欠陥を合格にせず、矛盾・根拠不足は保留とする。正常・欠陥各1件の合成較正で判定2件が実行検査と一致し、反例も実行確認した。初回の読取り拒否と再試行の費用も保存した。6分類 A/B の実測や非劣性の証明とは数えない。追加モデル実行の扱いはこの明示許可へ更新するが、tag・Release は開始しない。


## 2026-10-18：中間成果で終了しない操作者への補正

PR #97 を main `0e687eeb5d389872c360bebc9b34918b448be428` に統合した。ADR-0040 に判断理由を記録し、共通原稿で担当の終了とユーザーの最終依頼の完了を分けた。費用への懸念には冗長な評価・再試行・報告を減らすことで対応し、停止指示や実際の上限到達なしに全作業を止めない。既存証拠から修正を決められる場合は、追加の探索評価より修正を優先する。必要な権限・安全・予算の確認は維持する。

操作 skill は 1.3.1 とし、利用者・Runtime 文書を更新した。個人環境の skill は自動更新していない。CLI package の全テストと PR の必須 CI は成功したが、これらは原稿の配線・既存契約の回帰であり、モデルの継続判断や全体費用の改善を証明しない。この補正のための追加モデル評価は行っていない。

最終ゴールの達成後は、判断・決定・結果に合わせて ADR・Issue・milestone・PR を整合させ、コミットを保存してから完成を宣言する。中間成果の公開だけでは完成としない。

本 Issue の全工程での行動品質・費用改善は未判定のため、Issue と milestone は OPEN を維持する。以前の6分類の初期判断は取得済みだが、全工程の回答反映・拒否後停止・修正後検証・外側操作者を含む費用の証拠には置き換えない。追加評価を自動的に開始する決定でもない。


## 最終判定後の記録と完成報告

PR #98 / commit `9f5c551` で、最終受入条件を判定した後、依頼された ADR・Issue・milestone・PR を判断・根拠・結果に整合させ、コミットと必要な公開確認を終えてから完成を報告する規則を実装した。ADR-0040、利用者・Runtime 文書、操作 skill 1.3.2 を揃えた。未達条件を閉じず、依頼外の公開要件は増やさない。全リポジトリ検査は成功した。Controller に外部記録の自動更新機構を追加したものではなく、原稿の配線検査を行動・費用改善の実証とは扱わない。

6分類の課題・原稿切替・収集手順の準備と、初期判断 A/B 各1回の手順点検は実施済みとして整理する。外側操作者を固定した全工程比較ではなく、回答反映・拒否後停止・修正後検証は未測定である。比較の品質維持と全体効率改善は判定保留であり、Issue #90 と milestone #27 は OPEN を維持する。追加モデル評価は自動起動しない。


実装の公開は v0.4.0（#99 / PR #100 / milestone #28）として完了：https://github.com/hiono/taxion/releases/tag/v0.4.0 。本 milestone は行動品質・費用改善の実証を追跡し、未達条件を保持して OPEN とする。

raw.body:
## 目的

Job を継続単位とし、人と複数 Role が同じ目的・制約・成果・証拠を共有して、判断、相談、委譲、実行、独立レビュー、継続を行える協調モデルを完成させる。

本Issueは既存 Planner / Coder / Reviewer の固定実行フローや Clarification / ReviewFlow protocol の補修を目的としない。旧実装は参照資料であり、新モデルに適合する技術部品だけを再利用する。旧 domain model、旧認可モデル、旧実行経路が Job-native モデルを制約する場合は削除・置換する。互換性維持だけを理由に並行 runtime や fallback を残さない。

設計判断:
- [ADR-0077 Job 中心の Role 協調](https://github.com/hiono/taxion/blob/redesign/job-centered-role-collaboration/docs/develop/adr/0077-job-centered-role-collaboration.md)
- [ADR-0080 Job 境界と禁止副作用](https://github.com/hiono/taxion/blob/redesign/job-centered-role-collaboration/docs/develop/adr/0080-job-boundary-and-prohibited-effects.md)
- [ADR-0082 Job の開発作業を Git Worktree 単位で制御する](https://github.com/hiono/taxion/blob/redesign/job-centered-role-collaboration/docs/develop/adr/0082-job-workspace-parallelism-and-ownership.md)
- [設計ノート](https://github.com/hiono/taxion/blob/redesign/job-centered-role-collaboration/docs/develop/role-collaboration.md)
- [実装PR #292](https://github.com/hiono/taxion/pull/292)

## 全体再設計原則

本Issueは [ADR-0081: 再設計では旧設計の制約を温存せず、製品を作り直す](https://github.com/hiono/taxion/blob/redesign/job-centered-role-collaboration/docs/develop/adr/0081-rebuild-over-legacy-constraints.md) に従う。

**移行とは付け替えだけではない。作り直すことで製品は良くなっていく。**

旧モデルの責務が新モデルと矛盾する場合、旧コード・API・データ構造・テストを残すことを既定にしない。再利用するのは新しい不変条件に適合する技術的実装に限る。新しい不変条件からAPI・保存・Runtime・テストを再構築し、旧モデルとの互換性を目的にしない。実際の複数Role協調が成立し、利用者価値が向上したことを完成条件とする。

旧実装を一時的に残す場合は、具体的な依存・置換先・削除条件を示す。履歴保持は旧実行・認可経路の維持を意味しない。

## 基本モデル

- Job は目的、制約、承認済み境界、受入条件、成果、検証証拠、協調履歴を保持する永続的な作業単位とする。
- Role は Job を進める責務であり、固定順序・固定session寿命・静的なoperation ACLに拘束しない。
- RoleExecution は Role の個々の実行を表し、Jobの寿命と分離する。
- Role は Job Context と成果物を参照し、不完全な情報から専門的に判断する。可逆な作業は仮定と不確実性を示して進め、判断に不可欠な情報だけを相手 Role または人へ尋ねる。
- 質問、回答、判断、委譲、部分成果は同じ Job に記録し、担当 Role が回答を利用して続行できるようにする。
- Job内の独立したTaskを並行させる場合はTaskごとにGit Worktreeを割り当てる。異なるWorktreeのTaskはJob Graphの依存関係と承認済み上限の範囲で並行実行し、同じWorktree内のCoder / Reviewer / 修正担当は逐次引き継ぐ。独立性が不明なTaskは直列化する（ADR-0082）。
- Reviewer は Coder の実行終了後に同じ作業環境を引き継ぎ、固定成果物を独立 Context / session と read-only 境界で検証する。物理的な別 Worktree を常時要求しない。

## 認可・安全境界

- JobApproval は immutable Job revision に束縛された Job の唯一の権限根拠とする。会話、Task、RoleExecution、旧承認記録から権限を導出しない。
- Job は repository/resource、worktree/sandbox、file access、budget、deadline、禁止副作用、承認が必要な副作用、非秘密のRuntime設定参照を承認対象として保持する。開発実行はGit repositoryを前提とし、並行作業はGit Worktreeで分離する（ADR-0082）。
- 通常の可逆な作業は、承認済み Job の強制可能な境界内であれば operation 名や Role ごとの許可リストへの事前登録を要求しない。
- Controller は Job の同一性、承認revision、resource境界、同一Worktreeの単一所有権、Provider停止状態、Graph依存関係、禁止副作用、実行環境による封じ込め、予算、期限、provenanceを検証する。fencing tokenだけでProviderの直接filesystem writeを防げるとはみなさない。
- taxion doctor は既存のProject設定・Provider実行環境の診断責務を維持する。Git repositoryの利用要件と並行時のGit Worktree利用はREADMEで説明する。ready / Skillは操作手順を示すが、環境選択・所有権・認可を保証しない。Worktree操作はGitのnative操作を使用し、Taxion独自のVCS / Workspace engineを実装しない。
- 不明な tool 名だけを理由に拒否しない。影響を検査・封じ込めできない場合は、具体的な人間承認要求または拒否とする。
- 秘密情報の漏えい、Job境界外アクセス、権限昇格、sandbox escape、承認外の外部副作用、履歴・provenance改変、二重実行は fail-closed とする。
- ValidationCommands は承認済み文字列との完全一致を維持する。汎用 process.exec 能力を任意commandの許可に使わない。
- commit / push / release / publish は一律禁止しない。Jobの目的・対象・承認範囲・実行主体に照らして判定する。

## 旧実装の扱い

旧 Task / ReviewFlow / Clarification / Dispatch / role packet / Role operation allowlist は新モデルの制約としない。旧実行・認可経路を並行 runtime として残さず、Job-native の実行・認可・復旧モデルへ置き換える。旧データの保持・移行が必要な場合は、実行や認可を行わない明示的かつ loss-aware な履歴境界に限定する。旧承認を JobApproval に暗黙変換しない。

## 実装作業

1. Job、Task、RoleExecution、JobApproval、JobOutput、JobEvidence のdomain modelと不変条件を設計文書で確定する。旧runtimeへ先行実装しない。
2. Production caller、state mutation、Provider、bootstrap、restore / migration / recovery の全経路を監査し、旧実行権限の退役境界と復活経路を確定する。
3. Job-native経路への切替より先に、CLI / HTTP / Web / Controller / Runtime / Store / Graphの旧Task / Dispatch / ReviewFlow実行入口と、JSON bootstrap / snapshot restore / migration / recoveryによる再有効化を遮断する。旧承認はJob権限へ変換しない。
4. 旧実行面、fallback、旧Controller / Runtime contract、旧Graph mutator、旧Store経路、旧挙動だけを守るテスト・設定・help・運用手順を機能単位で削除する。必要な履歴は実行・認可を持たない形式で保持する。
5. 旧経路が退役した状態から、Job作成、PlanningAuthorization、JobApproval、Role handoff / reply / human resume、Provider stop observation、JobOutput / JobEvidence、完了・復旧を含むJob-native唯一経路を最小の縦方向スライスで再構築する。
6. 削除後の実コードと迂回路を基にGraph、aggregate、mutation boundaryを再検討する。ADR-0083は2026-11-16にJobAggregate境界、協調関係、command model、Provider / Worktree lifecycle invariantsについてAccepted。SQLite schemaとserialization mechanicsは実装判断としてADRに適合させる。

8. その後に限り、Task Worktree ownership、stop-proof-bound transfer、quarantine/release、schedulerを設計・実装する。
 
## 受入れ条件

- [ ] JobとRoleExecutionの寿命・責務が分離され、Jobが協調履歴と成果の正本となる。
- [ ] Roleの実行順序やprovider sessionの都合に依存せず、同じJobを継続できる。
- [ ] Roleが必要に応じて自然言語で他Roleへ依頼・質問でき、回答・部分成果を元のJobで利用して続行できる。
- [ ] 情報不足、任意metadata欠落、自然言語表現差だけでhandoffを拒否しない。
- [ ] JobApprovalだけがJob権限の根拠となり、会話・Task・旧approvalから権限を継承しない。
- [ ] 通常のin-bound操作はoperation/Role allowlistへの事前登録を要求せず、Job境界と禁止副作用で制御される。
- [ ] Job境界外アクセス、secret exfiltration、権限昇格、sandbox escape、未承認外部副作用、二重実行を拒否する。
- [ ] Start / Resume / Send / tool preflightで同一の認可不変条件が強制される。
- [ ] 旧 Task / ReviewFlow の実行・認可経路が並行runtimeとして残らず、履歴データ処理が権限を付与しない。
- [ ] 同一Git Worktree内のmutating RoleExecutionは逐次実行され、Provider停止・結果保存・成果物固定後にのみ所有権が移る。WAITINGだけでは解放しない。停止状態が不明なWorktreeは再利用せず隔離する。
- [ ] 独立したGit WorktreeのTaskはJob Graphの依存関係が解決した場合に並行実行する。独立性が不明なTaskは直列化し、Worktree間の変更競合は成果固定後の統合作業で明示的に解決する。Repository共通Git metadataの更新は直列化する。
- [ ] Provider停止を確認できない場合にWorktreeの所有権を移さず、クラッシュ後も停止不明のWorktreeを再利用しない。Controllerは古いownerによる状態更新・成果確定を拒否する。
- [ ] READMEがGit repositoryとGit Worktreeの利用要件を説明する。doctorは既存責務を維持し、ready / Skillは操作手順を示す。ControllerがWorktree所有権とJob境界を強制する。
- [ ] ReviewerがCoderの終了後に同じ固定成果物を独立Context / sessionとread-only境界で検証し、Job完了条件が全状態変更・保存・復元経路で強制される。
- [ ] 合成テストと実モデルE2Eを区別し、Planner/Coder/Reviewerの実協調と成果反映を確認する。

## 2026-11-15 concurrency scope clarification

ADR-0082の見直しにより、並行実行の前提を実際の開発利用環境に限定する。Git repositoryを必須とし、独立Taskは別Git Worktreeへ割り当てる。同じWorktreeのRoleは逐次実行し、Task間の独立性が不明な場合は直列化する。Worktree間の意味的競合は成果固定後の統合作業で解決する。全filesystem accessを対象とする汎用lock graph、任意の同一Worktree同時編集、fencing tokenだけによる物理書込み防止は採用しない。

Go race detectorは維持するが、検証対象はサポートするStore / Controller / Providerの並行経路、独立Worktreeの同時実行、同一Worktreeの二重所有拒否、Repository共通Git metadataの直列化とする。サポートしない同一Worktreeの複数mutating Role同時編集を、製品の正常な利用シナリオとして網羅するテストは追加しない。README、ADR-0077、ADR-0080、ADR-0027、ADR-0032およびJob実行設計文書はADR-0082に整合させた。


## 2026-11-15 Job-first Planner and replacement order

The request lifecycle is Job-first. The original request creates a durable Job before any Planner model call. The explicit user-invoked intake records a separate, immutable `PlanningAuthorization` for one Taskless Planner RoleExecution. This grant is limited to bounded planning and read-only context acquisition; it is not JobApproval, does not activate the Job, and cannot authorize implementation Tasks, writes, validation, commit, publication, credentials, network or external mutation. If the Provider cannot enforce read-only repository access, use an immutable snapshot / explicit context documents or deny repository reads.

The Planner's questions, answers, proposal revisions, usage and execution provenance belong to the same Job. The full implementation JobContract is proposed after planning and requires explicit approval of its exact revision hash. Only that JobApproval authorizes implementation Task / RoleExecution creation. Planner output and human clarification do not widen PlanningAuthorization or grant implementation authority.

The implementation order is fixed and deletion-first:

1. Complete the production caller, mutation, Provider, bootstrap, restore, migration and recovery audit.
2. Retire old Task / Dispatch / ReviewFlow execution authority and block every path that could reactivate it.
3. Remove old execution surfaces, fallbacks, and tests that exist only to preserve rejected legacy behavior. Keep required historical facts only behind a non-executable read boundary.
4. Rebuild the required Job-native user journey through one canonical path, including planning, approval, Role collaboration, human wait/reply/resume, Provider stop observation, results/evidence and recovery.
5. Perform clean refactoring after old-path removal, then implement the accepted ADR-0083 aggregate, command, Provider and Worktree lifecycle invariants. Physical SQLite schema and serialization remain implementation choices constrained by the ADR.
6. Only then design and implement Task Worktree ownership, stop-proof-bound transfer, quarantine/release and scheduling.

The recipient RoleExecution scope on handoff must be explicit: Taskless Job scope or a concrete Task belonging to the same Job. It must never inherit the source TaskID implicitly. Portable snapshot / restore must reject active or uncertain Job RoleExecutions unless independently persisted Provider stop observation and result/evidence reconciliation prove quiescence. Existing tests that assert implicit Task inheritance or only test Taskless Planner under an already approved Job are transitional tests and must be replaced with these new acceptance cases.
